   456	def apply_fields(entries: list[dict], name: str, fields: dict) -> list[str]:
   457	    """Apply ``{field: value}`` to one entry; returns one note per change.
   458	
   459	    The whole set is type-checked before anything is mutated, so a directive
   460	    with one bad field changes nothing at all.
   461	    """
   462	    entry = find(entries, name)
   463	    typed = [coerce(field, value) for field, value in fields.items()]
   464	    candidate = dict(entry)
   465	    changes: list[str] = []
   466	    for canonical, value in typed:
   467	        before = candidate.get(canonical)
   468	        candidate[canonical] = value
   469	        if before != value:
   470	            changes.append(f"{canonical} {before!r} -> {value!r}")
   471	    checked = validate_entry(candidate, f"account {name}")
   472	    entry.clear()
   473	    entry.update(checked)
   474	    return changes
   475	
   476	
   477	def add(entries: list[dict], name: str, *, endpoint: str, codex_home: str,
   478	        ceiling: int, label: str = "", reserved: int = 0, note: str = "",
   479	        enabled: bool = True) -> dict:
   480	    if any(entry["name"] == name for entry in entries):
   481	        raise AccountsError(f"account {name!r} already exists; use 'set' to change it")
   482	    entry = validate_entry({
   483	        "name": name, "label": label or name, "endpoint": endpoint,
   484	        "codex_home": codex_home, "ceiling": ceiling,
   485	        "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": enabled, "note": note,
   486	    }, f"account {name}")
   487	    entries.append(entry)
   488	    return entry
   489	
   490	
   491	def remove(entries: list[dict], name: str) -> dict:
   492	    entry = find(entries, name)
   493	    if len(entries) == 1:
   494	        raise AccountsError(
   495	            f"{name!r} is the only account; removing it would leave a file that "
   496	            "dispatches nowhere. Disable it instead, or add its replacement first.")
   497	    entries.remove(entry)
   498	    return entry
   499	
   500	
   501	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   502	# The owner-inbox comment channel
   503	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   504	
   505	def parse_directives(text: str) -> list[dict]:
   506	    """Every ``ACCOUNTS:`` line of a comment, parsed or rejected by name.
   507	
   508	    Returns one record per directive line::
   509	
   510	        {"raw": "...", "name": "second", "fields": {"ceiling": "20"}, "error": ""}
   511	
   512	    A record with a non-empty ``error`` is reported back to the owner rather than
   513	    applied, so a typo is answered instead of ignored.  Nothing outside an
   514	    ``ACCOUNTS:`` line is looked at: the rest of the comment is prose.
   515	    """
   516	    out: list[dict] = []
   517	    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
   518	        match = DIRECTIVE_RE.match(line)
   519	        if not match:
   520	            continue
   521	        record = {"raw": sanitize(line.strip(), 200), "name": "", "fields": {},
   522	                  "error": ""}
   523	        tokens = match.group("rest").split()
   524	        name = tokens[0] if tokens else ""
   525	        if not NAME_RE.match(name or ""):
   526	            record["error"] = (f"the first word after 'ACCOUNTS:' must be an account "
   527	                               f"name matching {NAME_RE.pattern}, got {name!r}")
   528	            out.append(record)
   529	            continue
   530	        record["name"] = name
   531	        for token in tokens[1:]:
   532	            assignment = ASSIGN_RE.match(token)
   533	            if not assignment:
   534	                record["error"] = (f"{token!r} is not a 'field=value' assignment; the "
   535	                                   "form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> "
   536	                                   "[reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   537	                break
   538	            key = assignment.group("key").lower()
   539	            if key not in DIRECTIVE_FIELDS:
   540	                record["error"] = (f"field {key!r} may not be set from a comment; this "
   541	                                   f"channel carries {', '.join(DIRECTIVE_FIELDS)} only "
   542	                                   "(an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host "
   543	                                   "and is set with accounts.sh)")
   544	                break
   545	            record["fields"][key] = assignment.group("value")
   546	        if not record["error"] and not record["fields"]:
   547	            record["error"] = ("no field to set; the form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> "
   548	                               "ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   549	        out.append(record)
   550	    return out
   551	
   552	
   553	def apply_directives(text: str, *, root: Path | None = None, actor: str,
   554	                     origin: str = "") -> list[str]:
   555	    """Apply every directive of one comment; returns the owner-facing lines.
   556	
   557	    Each line begins with ``applied:`` or ``rejected:`` and names the account and
   558	    what changed, so the confirmation reply says exactly what took effect.  A
   559	    rejected directive never blocks the others: the owner gets one answer per
   560	    line they wrote.
   561	    """
   562	    directives = parse_directives(text)
   563	    if not directives:
   564	        return []
   565	    entries = load(root)
   566	    if entries is None:
   567	        return [f"rejected: {record['raw']} — no {accounts_path(root)} on the host yet; "
   568	                "the run brief has not been applied" for record in directives]
   569	    results: list[str] = []
   570	    dirty = False
   571	    for record in directives:
   572	        if record["error"]:
   573	            results.append(f"rejected: {record['raw']} — {record['error']}")
   574	            continue
   575	        try:
   576	            changes = apply_fields(entries, record["name"], record["fields"])
   577	        except AccountsError as exc:
   578	            results.append(f"rejected: {record['raw']} — {exc}")
   579	            continue
   580	        dirty = True
   581	        results.append(f"applied: {record['name']} " +
   582	                       ("; ".join(changes) if changes
   583	                        else "already at the requested values"))
   584	    if dirty:
   585	        save(entries, root=root, actor=actor, action="inbox",
   586	             detail=f"{origin}: " + " | ".join(results),
   587	             source=f"owner inbox comment {origin}".strip())
   588	    return results
   589	
   590	
   591	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   592	# Rendering
   593	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   594	
   595	def _derived_state(root: Path | None = None) -> tuple[dict[str, int | None], dict[str, dict]]:
   596	    """The cap files and ``capacity/health.json``, both optional, never fatal.
   597	
   598	    They are written by the capacity controller next to the accounts file.  The
   599	    owner's first-line command has to show them: a key can be ``enabled`` in
   600	    their own file and still be cap 0 because a probe says the endpoint is down
   601	    or the key is invalid, and "why is nothing running on this key?" must be
   602	    answerable from ``accounts.sh list`` rather than from
   603	    ``capacity_controller.py status`` on the host.
   604	    """
   605	    base = (root or cache_root()) / "watchdog"
   606	    caps: dict[str, int | None] = {}
   607	    for path in base.glob("max-codex-*"):
   608	        if not path.is_file() or path.name == "max-codex":
   609	            continue
   610	        try:
   611	            caps[path.name[len("max-codex-"):]] = int(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
   612	        except (OSError, ValueError):
   613	            caps[path.name[len("max-codex-"):]] = None
   614	    try:
   615	        document = json.loads((base / "capacity" / "health.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   616	        health = document.get("accounts") if isinstance(document, dict) else None
   617	    except (OSError, ValueError):
   618	        health = None
   619	    return caps, health if isinstance(health, dict) else {}
   620	
   621	
   622	def render_table(entries: list[dict], root: Path | None = None) -> str:
   623	    caps, health = _derived_state(root)
   624	    width = max((len(entry["name"]) for entry in entries), default=4)
   625	    lines = []
   626	    for entry in entries:
   627	        name = entry["name"]
   628	        share = entry["ceiling"] - entry["external_reserved"]
   629	        # An ABSENT cap file is a hard 0 to `account_router.effective_caps`, so
   630	        # it is rendered as 0 with the reason, never omitted and never "unknown".
   631	        cap = caps.get(name)
   632	        shown = "0 (no tick yet)" if cap is None else str(cap)
   633	        row = health.get(name) if isinstance(health.get(name), dict) else {}
   634	        state = str(row.get("state") or "") or ("-" if not row else "up")
   635	        lines.append(
   636	            f"{name:<{width}}  ceiling {entry['ceiling']:<4} reserved "
   637	            f"{entry['external_reserved']:<3} share {share:<4} cap {shown:<16} "
   638	            f"{'enabled ' if entry['enabled'] else 'DISABLED'} health {state:<9} "
   639	            f"{entry['label']} ({entry['endpoint']}, {entry['codex_home']})"
   640	            + (f"  reason: {row['reason']}" if row.get("reason") else "")
   641	            + (f"  note: {entry['note']}" if entry["note"] else ""))
   642	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   643	
   644	
   645	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   646	# CLI
   647	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   648	
   649	def _require_file(root: Path | None) -> list[dict]:
   650	    entries = load(root)
   651	    if entries is None:
   652	        raise AccountsError(
   653	            f"no accounts file at {accounts_path(root)}.\n"
   654	            "It is seeded from the run brief by 'local/bin/run_mode.py apply'; "
   655	            "run that first, or write the file by hand from the template in "
   656	            "local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md.")
   657	    return entries
   658	
   659	
   660	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
   661	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   662	        prog="accounts_file.py", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0],
   663	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
   664	    parser.add_argument("--actor", default=os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNTS_ACTOR")
   665	                        or os.environ.get("USER") or "operator",
   666	                        help="who is making the change (recorded in accounts.log)")
   667	    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
   668	
   669	    p = sub.add_parser("list", help="every entry")
   670	    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
   671	
   672	    p = sub.add_parser("get", help="one entry, or one field of it")
   673	    p.add_argument("name")
   674	    p.add_argument("field", nargs="?")
   675	
   676	    p = sub.add_parser("set", help="change one field of one entry")
   677	    p.add_argument("name")
   678	    p.add_argument("field")
   679	    p.add_argument("value")
   680	
   681	    for word in ("enable", "disable"):
   682	        p = sub.add_parser(word, help=f"{word} one account")
   683	        p.add_argument("name")
   684	        p.add_argument("--note", default=None, help="replace the entry's note")
   685	
   686	    p = sub.add_parser("add", help="add a key")
   687	    p.add_argument("name")
   688	    p.add_argument("--endpoint", required=True)
   689	    p.add_argument("--codex-home", required=True)
   690	    p.add_argument("--ceiling", type=int, required=True)
   691	    p.add_argument("--label", default="")
   692	    p.add_argument("--reserved", type=int, default=0)
   693	    p.add_argument("--note", default="")
   694	    p.add_argument("--disabled", action="store_true",
   695	                   help="add the entry without enabling it yet")
   696	
   697	    p = sub.add_parser("remove", help="drop a key (cap 0 immediately)")
   698	    p.add_argument("name")
   699	
   700	    p = sub.add_parser("seed", help="write the file from a brief, if absent")
   701	    p.add_argument("--brief-accounts", required=True,
   702	                   help="JSON file holding the brief's accounts array")
   703	    p.add_argument("--source", default="")
   704	
   705	    p = sub.add_parser("apply-directives", help="apply one ACCOUNTS: comment body")
   706	    p.add_argument("--text-file", required=True)
   707	    p.add_argument("--origin", default="")
   708	    return parser
   709	
   710	
   711	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   712	    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
   713	    root = None
   714	    try:
   715	        if args.cmd == "list":
   716	            entries = _require_file(root)
   717	            if args.json:
   718	                json.dump(entries, sys.stdout, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
   719	                sys.stdout.write("\n")
   720	            else:
   721	                sys.stdout.write(render_table(entries, root))
   722	            return 0
   723	        if args.cmd == "get":
   724	            entry = find(_require_file(root), args.name)
   725	            if args.field:
   726	                canonical = FIELD_ALIASES.get(args.field.lower(), args.field.lower())
   727	                if canonical not in entry:
   728	                    raise AccountsError(f"unknown field {args.field!r}; an entry carries "
   729	                                        f"{', '.join(ENTRY_KEYS)}")
   730	                sys.stdout.write(f"{entry[canonical]}\n")
   731	            else:
   732	                json.dump(entry, sys.stdout, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
   733	                sys.stdout.write("\n")
   734	            return 0
   735	        if args.cmd == "set":
   736	            entries = _require_file(root)
   737	            changes = apply_fields(entries, args.name, {args.field: args.value})
   738	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="set",
   739	                 detail=f"{args.name}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or "no change"),
   740	                 source="accounts.sh set")
   741	            sys.stdout.write(f"{args.name}: {'; '.join(changes) or 'no change'}\n")
   742	            return 0
   743	        if args.cmd in ("enable", "disable"):
   744	            entries = _require_file(root)
   745	            fields: dict = {"enabled": args.cmd == "enable"}
   746	            if args.note is not None:
   747	                fields["note"] = args.note
   748	            changes = apply_fields(entries, args.name, fields)
   749	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action=args.cmd,
   750	                 detail=f"{args.name}: " + ("; ".join(changes) or "no change"),
   751	                 source=f"accounts.sh {args.cmd}")
   752	            sys.stdout.write(f"{args.name}: {'; '.join(changes) or 'no change'}\n")
   753	            return 0
   754	        if args.cmd == "add":
   755	            entries = _require_file(root)
   756	            entry = add(entries, args.name, endpoint=args.endpoint,
   757	                        codex_home=args.codex_home, ceiling=args.ceiling,
   758	                        label=args.label, reserved=args.reserved, note=args.note,
   759	                        enabled=not args.disabled)
   760	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="add",
   761	                 detail=f"{entry['name']} endpoint={entry['endpoint']} "
   762	                        f"ceiling={entry['ceiling']} enabled={entry['enabled']}",
   763	                 source="accounts.sh add")
   764	            sys.stdout.write(f"added {entry['name']} (ceiling {entry['ceiling']}, "
   765	                             f"{'enabled' if entry['enabled'] else 'disabled'})\n")
   766	            return 0
   767	        if args.cmd == "remove":
   768	            entries = _require_file(root)
   769	            entry = remove(entries, args.name)
   770	            save(entries, root=root, actor=args.actor, action="remove",
   771	                 detail=f"{entry['name']} (ceiling {entry['ceiling']})",
   772	                 source="accounts.sh remove")
   773	            sys.stdout.write(f"removed {entry['name']}; its cap is 0 from the next "
   774	                             "controller tick\n")
   775	            return 0
   776	        if args.cmd == "seed":
   777	            raw = json.loads(Path(args.brief_accounts).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   778	            rows = raw.get("accounts") if isinstance(raw, dict) else raw
   779	            written, path = seed(rows, root=root, source=args.source)
   780	            sys.stdout.write(f"{'wrote' if written else 'kept existing'} {path}\n")
   781	            return 0
   782	        if args.cmd == "apply-directives":
   783	            text = Path(args.text_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   784	            lines = apply_directives(text, root=root, actor=args.actor,
   785	                                     origin=args.origin)
   786	            sys.stdout.write("\n".join(lines) + ("\n" if lines else ""))
   787	            return 0
   788	    except UnknownAccount as exc:
   789	        sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_file.py: {exc}\n")
   790	        return 3
   791	    except (AccountsError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
   792	        sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_file.py: {exc}\n")
   793	        return 2
   794	    return 2
   795	
   796	
   797	if __name__ == "__main__":
   798	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The owner's GitHub control channel for the live accounts file.
     3	
     4	The shell is not always at hand.  A comment on the owner inbox issue in the
     5	fixed form::
     6	
     7	    ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20
     8	    ACCOUNTS: third enabled=false
     9	
    10	is applied to ``watchdog/accounts.json`` by the janitor at its next sweep and
    11	answered with one reply saying exactly what took effect::
    12	
    13	    applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20
    14	    rejected: ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=10 — no account named 'fourth'; the file
    15	    has primary, second, third
    16	
    17	Three rules make this safe enough to be a control channel rather than a
    18	conversation:
    19	
    20	* **The author must be the repository owner.**  The login is taken from
    21	  ``MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN``, then from the ``Repository owner login:`` line in
    22	  ``local/README.md``, then from the owner half of the repository slug.  A
    23	  directive from anyone else is never applied; it is answered with a
    24	  ``rejected:`` line naming the author, so an attempt is visible rather than
    25	  silent.
    26	* **One reply per comment, and applying is once.**  Each answered comment gets a
    27	  reply carrying ``<!-- mipstarre-accounts comment=<id> -->``; a comment that
    28	  already has one is skipped entirely, so a sweep every minute does not re-apply
    29	  a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell.
    30	* **The channel carries ceilings, reserved slots, the enabled flag and a note —
    31	  nothing else.**  An endpoint or a codex home is a path on the owner's host and
    32	  is set with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, where a typo cannot travel through a
    33	  public comment.  ``accounts_file.py`` owns the parsing and the validation, so
    34	  this channel and the CLI cannot disagree about what a valid entry is.
    35	
    36	Comment bodies are untrusted text (``local/protocols/issues-prs.md`` §4): only
    37	lines matching ``ACCOUNTS:`` are read at all, every value is validated before
    38	anything is written, and nothing is ever interpolated into a shell.
    39	
    40	Usage::
    41	
    42	    accounts_inbox.py [--issue N] [--dry-run] [--limit N]
    43	
    44	Exit codes: 0 (including "nothing to do"), 2 a GitHub or run-mode failure.
    45	"""
    46	
    47	from __future__ import annotations
    48	
    49	import argparse
    50	import json
    51	import os
    52	import re
    53	import sys
    54	from datetime import datetime, timezone
    55	from pathlib import Path

    61	    sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_inbox.py: cannot import gh_common.py ({exc}).\n")
    62	    raise SystemExit(2)

    64	import accounts_file  # noqa: E402

    68	MARKER = "mipstarre-accounts"
    69	
    70	#: The line ``local/README.md`` carries, and the only thing read from it.
    71	OWNER_LINE_RE = re.compile(
    72	    r"Repository owner login:\s*\**\s*`?([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38})`?")
    73	
    74	#: How many of the newest comments are looked at at all.  A COUNT bound only;
    75	#: the temporal bound below is the one the staleness rule needs.
    76	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 40
    77	
    78	#: Comments older than this are not answered.  A directive the janitor never saw
    79	#: — the daemon was down for a day — is stale capacity advice, and applying it
    80	#: hours later would be worse than ignoring it.  The count cap alone did not
    81	#: implement that rule: the owner inbox issue is permissions-only and low
    82	#: traffic, so far fewer than `DEFAULT_LIMIT` comments exist and every
    83	#: `ACCOUNTS:` comment ever written stayed in scope forever.  With the pipeline
    84	#: deliberately paused, the janitor's first sweep after a resume would have
    85	#: applied the whole backlog at once — including `enabled=false`, which is cap 0

    93	def owner_login(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:

    99	    try:

   101	    except OSError:

   103	    if match:
   104	        return match.group(1), f"{readme} (Repository owner login:)"

   109	def comment_age_min(row: dict, now: datetime | None = None) -> float | None:
   110	    """Age of a comment in minutes from its ``created_at``; ``None`` when absent.
   111	
   112	    ``None`` — no timestamp, or one that does not parse — is treated as NOT
   113	    stale by `sweep`.  The REST API always supplies ``created_at``, so a missing
   114	    one means an unusual payload rather than an old comment, and refusing to
   115	    answer it would silently drop a directive the owner did write.
   116	    """
   117	    raw = row.get("created_at")
   118	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
   119	        return None
   120	    try:
   121	        moment = datetime.fromisoformat(raw.strip().replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   122	    except ValueError:
   123	        return None
   124	    if moment.tzinfo is None:
   125	        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   126	    return ((now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)) - moment).total_seconds() / 60.0

   277	        raise ControllerError(f"{path}: run mode is missing or unreadable ({exc}); apply the "
   278	                              "owner's brief first: run_mode.py apply --brief PATH") from exc
   279	    _require(isinstance(mode, dict), f"{path}: run mode must be an object")
   280	    raw = mode.get("accounts")

   282	        entries = [dict(value, name=value.get("name", key)) for key, value in raw.items()

   296	                        minimum=0)

   298	                 f"{path}: {name}.external_reserved ({reserved}) exceeds nominal_limit ({nominal})")
   299	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("enabled", True), bool),
   300	                 f"{path}: {name}.enabled must be true or false")
   301	        _require(isinstance(entry.get("endpoint") or name, str),
   302	                 f"{path}: {name}.endpoint must be a string")

   315	def overlay_live_accounts(from_mode: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], str]:
   316	    """Replace the mode's account list with the owner's live file when it exists.
   317	
   318	    THE HOT RELOAD.  ``load_run_mode`` runs once per tick, so the ceilings, the
   319	    reserved slots and the enabled flags the controller uses are at most one tick
   320	    (60 s) old.  The live file is authoritative in full: an entry the owner
   321	    removed is gone from the tick that follows, which is cap 0 and no probe —
   322	    the same as ``enabled: false``, and deliberately so.
   323	
   324	    An unreadable or invalid file is a HARD failure, like a malformed run mode:
   325	    the caller exits nonzero and leaves the cap files exactly as they are.
   326	    Falling back to the brief would silently restore a ceiling the owner has just
   327	    lowered, which is the one behaviour this file exists to remove.
   328	    """
   329	    try:
   330	        entries = accounts_file.load()
   331	    except accounts_file.AccountsError as exc:
   332	        raise ControllerError(
   333	            f"{exc}\nThe cap files are untouched. Fix the field this message names "
   334	            f"(results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list), or delete "
   335	            f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} to fall back to the brief.") from exc
   336	    if entries is None:
   337	        return from_mode, "run-mode.json (no accounts.json yet)"
   338	    live: dict[str, dict] = {}
   339	    for entry in entries:
   340	        name = entry["name"]
   341	        ceiling = entry["ceiling"]
   342	        reserved = min(entry["external_reserved"], ceiling)
   343	        live[name] = {"name": name, "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   344	                      "label": entry["label"], "nominal_limit": ceiling,
   345	                      "codex_home": entry["codex_home"],
   346	                      "external_reserved": reserved, "enabled": entry["enabled"],
   347	                      "note": entry["note"]}
   348	    _require(bool(live), f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()}: no account entries")
   349	    return live, str(accounts_file.accounts_path())

   374	def read_session_rows(path: Path, since: datetime, *, tail_bytes: int = TAIL_BYTES) -> list[dict]:
   375	    """Rows newer than *since* from the tail of ``sessions.jsonl``.
   376	
   377	    The registry grows for the life of the project and the counters never look
   378	    back further than five minutes.  A malformed row is skipped, not fatal.
   379	    """
   380	    try:
   381	        size = path.stat().st_size
   382	        with path.open("rb") as handle:
   383	            if size > tail_bytes:
   384	                handle.seek(size - tail_bytes)
   385	                handle.readline()  # drop the partial row the seek landed inside
   386	            blob = handle.read()
   387	    except OSError:
   388	        return []
   389	    rows = []
   390	    for line in blob.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
   391	        try:
   392	            row = json.loads(line)
   393	        except ValueError:
   394	            continue
   395	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   396	            continue
   397	        moment = parse_ts(row.get("end")) or parse_ts(row.get("start")) or parse_ts(row.get("ts"))
   398	        if moment is not None and moment >= since:
   399	            rows.append(dict(row, _ts=moment))
   400	    return rows

   403	def attribution_map(accounts: dict[str, dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
   404	    """``token -> account`` for failure attribution, plus the ambiguous tokens.
   405	
   406	    Account NAMES are unique by construction and always map to themselves.  An
   407	    endpoint or a label may legitimately be shared — the owner's topology is one
   408	    to three endpoints with one or two keys on each — and a shared token cannot
   409	    say which key refused, so it is DROPPED rather than resolved to the last
   410	    entry that claimed it.  Dropping it costs nothing: every row the dispatcher
   411	    writes carries ``account``, which `observe` now reads first.  Keeping it was
   412	    an active harm — it moved a refusal, and at ``disable_threshold`` 1 a whole
   413	    key, onto a key that had done nothing.
   414	    """
   415	    endpoints: dict[str, str] = {name: name for name in accounts}
   416	    claimed: dict[str, str] = {}
   417	    ambiguous: set[str] = set()
   418	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   419	        for token in (entry.get("endpoint"), entry.get("label")):
   420	            if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or token in endpoints:
   421	                continue  # an account name always outranks another key's label
   422	            if claimed.setdefault(token, name) != name:
   423	                ambiguous.add(token)
   424	    endpoints.update({token: owner for token, owner in claimed.items()
   425	                      if token not in ambiguous})
   426	    return endpoints, sorted(ambiguous)

   429	def observe(rows: list[dict], name: str, endpoints: dict[str, str], roles: dict[str, str],
   430	            now: datetime, *, counter_window_s: int, fivexx_window_s: int,
   431	            disabling: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict:
   432	    """Refusal, death and key-invalidating counters for one account.
   433	
   434	    A ``failure_class`` the policy does not name — including the literal
   435	    ``unknown`` — is counted in neither direction, so a reworded provider message
   436	    leaves the cap where a hand-set cap would have been instead of collapsing it.
   437	
   438	    ``disabling`` names the classes that say the KEY is unusable rather than busy
   439	    (``auth``, ``insufficient_balance``).  They are collected separately, with
   440	    their detail, because the answer to them is "disable this key and say why",
   441	    not "lower the cap by a quarter".
   442	    """
   443	    bucket: dict[str, Any] = {"refusals": 0, "deaths": 0, "neutral": 0,
   444	                              "deaths_by_class": {}, "refusal_times": [], "fivexx_times": [],
   445	                              "disable_times": [], "disable_class": "", "disable_detail": ""}
   446	    counter_since = now - timedelta(seconds=counter_window_s)
   447	    fivexx_since = now - timedelta(seconds=fivexx_window_s)
   448	    for row in rows:
   449	        # ``account`` FIRST.  The dispatcher writes the name it actually routed
   450	        # to; an endpoint is shared by up to two keys in the owner's own topology
   451	        # (one to three endpoints, one or two keys each).  Matching the endpoint
   452	        # first attributed a refusal to whichever key happened to be written into
   453	        # the endpoint map last, so AIMD cut the innocent key while the refusing
   454	        # one crept up, and one `auth` row disabled the wrong key at threshold 1.
   455	        recorded_account = row.get("account")
   456	        if isinstance(recorded_account, str) and accounts_file.NAME_RE.match(recorded_account):
   457	            owner = (recorded_account
   458	                     if endpoints.get(recorded_account) == recorded_account else None)
   459	        else:
   460	            owner = next((endpoints[row[field]] for field in
   461	                          ("endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "key_label")
   462	                          if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in endpoints), None)
   463	        failure_class = row.get("failure_class")
   464	        if owner != name or not isinstance(failure_class, str) or not failure_class:
   465	            continue
   466	        if failure_class == "endpoint_5xx" and row["_ts"] >= fivexx_since:
   467	            bucket["fivexx_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   468	        if row["_ts"] < counter_since:
   469	            continue
   470	        if failure_class in disabling:
   471	            bucket["disable_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   472	            bucket["disable_class"] = failure_class
   473	            bucket["disable_detail"] = str(row.get("failure_detail") or "")[:120]
   474	        role = roles.get(failure_class, "neutral")
   475	        if role == "refusal":
   476	            bucket["refusals"] += 1
   477	            bucket["refusal_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   478	        elif role == "death":
   479	            bucket["deaths"] += 1
   480	            bucket["deaths_by_class"][failure_class] = \
   481	                bucket["deaths_by_class"].get(failure_class, 0) + 1
   482	        else:
   483	            bucket["neutral"] += 1
   484	    bucket["refusal_times"].sort()
   485	    bucket["fivexx_times"].sort()
   486	    bucket["disable_times"].sort()
   487	    return bucket

   552	def write_cap_files(caps: dict[str, int]) -> int:
   553	    """Write the legacy derived outputs; ``max-codex`` is mechanically the sum.
   554	
   555	    It therefore cannot disagree with the per-account files.  It is a display and
   556	    lane-parallelism value only: admission reads the per-account files
   557	    (``local/protocols/capacity.md`` §4).
   558	    """
   559	    effective = {name: int(value) for name, value in caps.items()}
   560	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   560	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   561	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   562	    # A cap file for an account that has dropped out of the configured set is
   563	    # ZEROED, not deleted.  Deleting it would break the "never an empty read"
   564	    # property; leaving its old number is worse still, because that stale file is
   565	    # exactly what `account_router.account_names()` picks up from its
   566	    # ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable — a key the owner
   567	    # removed would go on being admitted at the ceiling it had when they removed
   568	    # it.  The two historical names keep a file unconditionally, so a reader that
   569	    # predates this layer still finds a number.
   570	    stale = sorted(path.name[len("max-codex-"):] for path in
   571	                   directory.glob("max-codex-*")
   572	                   if path.is_file() and path.name != "max-codex"
   573	                   and path.name[len("max-codex-"):] not in effective)
   574	    for name in (*DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS, *stale,
   575	                 *(name for name in effective if name not in DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)):
   576	        _write_cap_file(directory / f"max-codex-{name}", effective.get(name, 0))
   577	    _write_cap_file(directory / "max-codex", sum(effective.values()))
   578	    return sum(effective.values())

   621	def update_health(account: str, health: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, now: datetime,
   622	                  *, no_probe: bool, codex_home: str, probe_timeout_s: int) -> str:
   623	    """Advance the endpoint health machine one tick; returns what it did.
   624	
   625	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a
   626	    5xx never runs the AIMD arithmetic.
   627	
   628	    Two kinds of trip, one machine.  ``endpoint_5xx`` says the ENDPOINT is down
   629	    and needs ``fivexx_threshold`` deaths inside ``fivexx_window_s`` — a single
   630	    502 is noise.  ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance`` say the KEY is unusable
   631	    and trip at ``disable_threshold`` (1): a `401` is not a statistic, and
   632	    retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead
   633	    sessions.  Both write the REASON into the health file, because "cap 0" with
   634	    no reason is the state the owner had to diagnose by reading captures on
   635	    2026-09-12; the way back is the same half-open probe, with the key-invalid
   636	    backoff starting longer (``disable_backoff_s``) since a key does not become
   637	    valid again in thirty seconds.
   638	    """
   639	    fivexx = len(counters["fivexx_times"])
   640	    disabling = len(counters.get("disable_times") or ())
   641	    base = knobs["probe_backoff_s"]
   642	    disable_base = max(base, int(knobs.get("disable_backoff_s",
   643	                                           _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_backoff_s"])))
   644	    health.update(consecutive_5xx=fivexx, key_failures=disabling, updated=ts(now))
   645	    if health["state"] != "down":
   646	        if disabling >= int(knobs.get("disable_threshold",
   647	                                      _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_threshold"])):
   648	            detail = counters.get("disable_detail") or ""
   649	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0,
   650	                          backoff_s=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]),
   651	                          reason=f"{counters.get('disable_class') or 'key'}: "
   652	                                 f"{detail or 'the key was refused'}",
   653	                          disabled_by=counters.get("disable_class") or "key",
   654	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(
   655	                              seconds=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]))))
   656	            return "trip"
   657	        if fivexx >= knobs["fivexx_threshold"]:
   658	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, backoff_s=base,
   659	                          reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} deaths in "
   660	                                 f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s",
   661	                          disabled_by="endpoint_5xx",
   662	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base)))
   663	            return "trip"
   664	        if fivexx:
   665	            if health["state"] != "degraded":
   666	                health.update(state="degraded", since=ts(now),
   667	                              reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} death(s) in "
   668	                                     f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s, below the "
   669	                                     f"threshold of {knobs['fivexx_threshold']}")
   670	            return "degraded"
   671	        if health["state"] != "up":
   672	            health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), reason="")
   673	            return "clear"
   674	        return "none"
   675	    if no_probe:  # an operator hold, or a key the brief disabled
   676	        return "probe-held"
   677	    due = parse_ts(health.get("next_probe_at"))
   678	    if due is not None and now < due:
   679	        return "probe-waiting"
   680	    ran, ok = _try_probe(account, codex_home, probe_timeout_s)
   681	    if not ran:
   682	        return "probe-inflight"
   683	    if not ok:

   701	def clamp(value: int, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> int:
   702	    """Into ``[floor, ceiling]``; the ceiling wins when the two cross."""

   706	def apply_aimd(account_state: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   707	               *, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> list[str]:
   708	    """Decrease first, so a refusal cannot be overtaken by an increase."""
   709	    notes: list[str] = []
   710	    aimd = knobs["aimd"]
   711	    window = timedelta(seconds=aimd["quiet_window_s"])
   712	    cap = int(account_state["cap"])
   713	    cursor = parse_ts(account_state.get("refusal_cursor"))
   714	    fresh = [moment for moment in counters["refusal_times"] if cursor is None or moment > cursor]
   715	    if fresh:
   716	        until = parse_ts(account_state.get("decrease_window_until"))
   717	        if until is None or now > until:
   718	            # The FIRST refusal of a window: step just under the concurrency that
   719	            # was refused.  ``live`` is sampled at the tick that observes it,
   720	            # which is the closest the controller gets to the moment of refusal —
   721	            # but when the refused sessions have already died it is 0 or 1, and a
   722	            # raw ``live - 1`` would collapse the cap to the floor and then climb
   723	            # back one slot per quiet window (an hour from 1 to 30 with the
   724	            # shipped defaults).  Fall back to what the account is KNOWN to have
   725	            # sustained before believing an instantaneous zero.
   726	            evidence = [value for value in
   727	                        (account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor"),
   728	                         account_state.get("measured_limit"))
   729	                        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)]
   730	            basis = live if live > 1 else max([live] + evidence)
   731	            cap = max(floor, min(cap, basis - 1))
   732	            account_state["decrease_window_until"] = ts(now + window)
   733	            notes.append(f"decrease(first) live={live} basis={basis} -> {cap}")
   734	            observed = basis
   735	        else:
   736	            cap = max(floor, math.ceil(cap * float(aimd["decrease"])))
   737	            notes.append(f"decrease(x{aimd['decrease']}) -> {cap}")
   738	            observed = live
   739	        account_state.update(refusal_cursor=ts(max(fresh)), quiet_since=None)
   740	        if observed >= 1:  # a zero census is not evidence that one slot refused
   741	            seen = account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor")
   742	            account_state["observed_refusal_floor"] = (
   743	                observed if seen is None else min(int(seen), observed))
   744	    # ``live >= cap - 1`` keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
   745	    # of headroom.
   746	    if (not counters["refusals"] and not counters["deaths"]
   747	            and account_state["health"] == "up" and live >= cap - 1):
   748	        started = parse_ts(account_state.get("quiet_since"))
   749	        if started is None:
   750	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   751	        elif now - started >= window:
   752	            if cap < ceiling:
   753	                cap = min(ceiling, cap + int(aimd["increase"]))
   754	                notes.append(f"increase -> {cap}")
   755	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   756	    else:
   757	        account_state["quiet_since"] = None
   758	    account_state["cap"] = clamp(cap, floor, ceiling)
   759	    return notes

   762	def update_measurement(account_state: dict, counters: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   763	                       *, measured_hold_s: int) -> None:
   764	    """The highest concurrency sustained *measured_hold_s* with no refusal or death."""
   765	    if counters["refusals"] or counters["deaths"]:
   766	        account_state.update(measured_since=None, measured_level=None)
   767	        return
   768	    started = parse_ts(account_state.get("measured_since"))
   769	    level = account_state.get("measured_level")
   770	    if started is None or not isinstance(level, int):
   771	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)
   772	        return
   773	    account_state["measured_level"] = min(int(level), live)
   774	    if now - started >= timedelta(seconds=measured_hold_s):
   775	        sustained, current = int(account_state["measured_level"]), account_state["measured_limit"]
   776	        if current is None or sustained > int(current):
   777	            account_state["measured_limit"] = sustained
   778	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)

   781	def refresh(account_state: dict, entry: dict, knobs: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
   782	    """Ceiling and floor from the brief and the policy; returns ``(floor, ceiling)``."""
   783	    ceiling = max(0, entry["nominal_limit"] - entry["external_reserved"])
   784	    floor = min(int(knobs["floor"]), ceiling)
   785	    account_state.update(nominal_limit=entry["nominal_limit"], floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling,
   786	                         external_reserved=entry["external_reserved"],
   787	                         enabled=entry["enabled"], endpoint=entry["endpoint"])

   791	def seed_cap(account_state: dict, floor: int, ceiling: int, entry: dict) -> int:
   792	    """Starting cap for a run: ``min(brief ceiling, last measured limit)``."""
   793	    if not entry["enabled"]:
   794	        return 0
   795	    measured = account_state.get("measured_limit")
   796	    return clamp(max(ceiling if measured is None else min(ceiling, int(measured)), 1),
   797	                 floor, ceiling)

   943	    ``primary``, and the shim then refused every dispatch to that key with exit

   952	    path = cache_root() / ACCOUNT_MODE_REL

   956	    except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
   957	        print(f"capacity controller: warning: cannot write {path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The owner's run briefing, validated once, and the mode file everything reads.
     3	
     4	One artifact states a run's capacity, schedule, speed and issue numbers: the
     5	brief the owner copies to ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/run-brief.json``
     6	from the committed template
     7	``results/telemetry/owner-tools/run-brief.template.json``.  ``apply`` validates
     8	it strictly and turns it into ``watchdog/run-mode.json``, the record every
     9	component reads through ``run_mode.py get KEY``.  No protocol, persona or
    10	script carries a literal cap, floor, cadence or issue number
    11	(``local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md``).
    12	
    13	Subcommands::
    14	
    15	    run_mode.py apply [--brief PATH] [--dry-run]
    16	    run_mode.py show [--json | --oneline]
    17	    run_mode.py get KEY
    18	    run_mode.py set speed fast|default [--dry-run]
    19	    run_mode.py pause [--reason TEXT]
    20	    run_mode.py resume
    21	
    22	``show --oneline`` renders the whole mode on one line; it is what the goal text
    23	(``owner-tools/goal-keeper.sh``) and the resume message
    24	(``owner-tools/owner-resume.sh``) carry, so neither has to name a number.
    25	
    26	``watchdog/account-mode`` is DERIVED from ``accounts[].enabled`` by ``apply``,
    27	``pause`` and ``resume`` — ``both`` when more than one account is enabled and
    28	``primary`` otherwise — because the deployed PATH shim reads it before it lets a
    29	dispatch use a second ``CODEX_HOME``.  It is not a field anyone briefs.
    30	
    31	``models.override`` is resolved against the speed tier rather than read
    32	literally: ``null`` means ``astra-all`` whenever ``run.speed`` is ``fast`` — in
    33	full speed mode every role, reviewers included, runs the hard model — and the
    34	published ``local/model-policy.json`` otherwise.  The literal ``"policy"`` keeps
    35	the published policy at any speed; ``"astra-all"`` forces the hard model at any
    36	speed.  ``set speed`` re-resolves it, so the tier and the models never disagree.
    37	
    38	Validation fails loudly at briefing time rather than at 05:00Z: an unknown
    39	key, a missing endpoint, a non-integer limit, ``external_reserved >=
    40	nominal_limit``, an occupancy target above 1, an unknown speed or model
    41	override, a non-positive issue number, or an account name outside
    42	``[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`` all exit 2 naming the offending key and the
    43	template path.  A missing brief is a hard error naming both paths — never
    44	silently zero and never silently unlimited capacity.
    45	
    46	**The brief seeds; the accounts file lives.**  ``apply`` writes
    47	``watchdog/accounts.json`` (``local/bin/accounts_file.py``) from the brief's
    48	``accounts`` block when that file does not exist, and **never overwrites an
    49	existing one**; where it exists it is what ``apply`` reads, so re-applying a
    50	brief to change the speed tier cannot undo the ceilings the owner has been
    51	editing all morning.  Any number of named accounts: ``primary`` and ``second``
    52	are ordinary entries, and a third key added with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh add``
    53	gets its own cap file, its own health and its own line in every report.

    56	where ``account_router.py``, the lane runner and ``status-snapshot.sh`` already

   256	def _require_int(value, key: str, *, minimum: int | None = None) -> int:
   257	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
   258	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be an integer, got {value!r}")
   259	    if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
   260	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be at least {minimum}, got {value}")

   264	def _require_text(value, key: str, *, pattern: re.Pattern | None = None) -> str:
   265	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
   266	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}")
   267	    text = value.strip()
   268	    if pattern is not None and not pattern.match(text):
   269	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} {text!r} does not match {pattern.pattern}")
   270	    return text

   273	def parse_timestamp(value, key: str) -> datetime:
   274	    """ISO-8601 instant; a bare `Z` is accepted on Python 3.10 too."""
   275	    text = _require_text(value, key)
   276	    candidate = text[:-1] + "+00:00" if text.endswith(("Z", "z")) else text
   277	    try:
   278	        moment = datetime.fromisoformat(candidate)
   279	    except ValueError as exc:
   280	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} {text!r} is not an ISO-8601 timestamp "
   281	                              f"(e.g. 2026-09-13T04:00:00Z): {exc}") from exc
   282	    if moment.tzinfo is None:
   283	        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   284	    return moment.astimezone(timezone.utc)

   287	def _validate_run(run: dict) -> dict:
   288	    _require_mapping(run, "run")
   289	    unknown = sorted(set(run) - set(RUN_KEYS_REQUIRED) - set(RUN_KEYS_OPTIONAL))
   290	    if unknown:
   291	        raise BriefError(f"run.{unknown[0]}",
   292	                         f"unknown key(s) under 'run': {', '.join(unknown)}")
   293	    missing = [key for key in RUN_KEYS_REQUIRED if key not in run]
   294	    if missing:
   295	        raise BriefError(f"run.{missing[0]}",
   296	                         f"'run' is missing: {', '.join(missing)}")
   297	
   298	    out: dict = {}
   299	    out["label"] = sanitize(_require_text(run["label"], "run.label"), 120)
   300	    out["start"] = parse_timestamp(run["start"], "run.start").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
   301	
   302	    cutoff = run["dispatch_cutoff"]
   303	    if isinstance(cutoff, str) and cutoff.strip().lower() == CUTOFF_OPEN:
   304	        out["dispatch_cutoff"] = CUTOFF_OPEN
   305	    else:
   306	        out["dispatch_cutoff"] = parse_timestamp(
   307	            cutoff, "run.dispatch_cutoff").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
   308	        if out["dispatch_cutoff"] <= out["start"]:
   309	            raise BriefError("run.dispatch_cutoff",
   310	                             f"run.dispatch_cutoff {out['dispatch_cutoff']} is not after "
   311	                             f"run.start {out['start']}; use the literal "
   312	                             f"{CUTOFF_OPEN!r} for an open-ended run")
   313	
   314	    out["pause_deadline_min"] = _require_int(
   315	        run["pause_deadline_min"], "run.pause_deadline_min", minimum=1)
   316	
   317	    speed = run["speed"]
   318	    if speed not in SPEEDS:
   319	        raise BriefError("run.speed",
   320	                         f"run.speed must be one of {SPEEDS}, got {speed!r}")
   321	    out["speed"] = speed
   322	
   323	    target = run["occupancy_target"]
   324	    if isinstance(target, bool) or not isinstance(target, (int, float)):
   325	        raise BriefError("run.occupancy_target",
   326	                         f"run.occupancy_target must be a number, got {target!r}")
   327	    if not 0 < float(target) <= 1:
   328	        raise BriefError("run.occupancy_target",
   329	                         f"run.occupancy_target must lie in (0, 1], got {target} — "
   330	                         "it is a fraction of the effective cap, not a worker count")
   331	    out["occupancy_target"] = float(target)
   332	
   333	    for key in ISSUE_KEYS:
   334	        out[key] = _require_int(run[key], f"run.{key}", minimum=1)
   335	    if len({out[key] for key in ISSUE_KEYS}) != len(ISSUE_KEYS):
   336	        raise BriefError("run.estimate_issue",
   337	                         "the progress log, the estimate issue and the owner inbox must be "
   338	                         "three different issues; the estimate issue carries exactly two "
   339	                         "rendered lines and nothing else (issues-prs.md section 6)")
   340	
   341	    if run.get("turn_max_min") is not None:
   342	        out["turn_max_min"] = _require_int(run["turn_max_min"], "run.turn_max_min", minimum=1)
   343	    else:
   344	        out["turn_max_min"] = TURN_MAX_MIN[speed]
   345	    out["estimate_cadence_min"] = ESTIMATE_CADENCE_MIN[speed]
   346	    out["main"] = _validate_main(run.get("main"))
   347	    return out

   449	
   450	    A briefed ``null`` resolves from the speed tier: ``fast`` is ``astra-all``,

   502	def read_brief(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, str]:
   503	    """Read, validate and digest the brief at *path*."""
   504	    if not path.exists():
   505	        raise BriefError("brief", f"no run brief at {path}\n{_template_hint()}\n"
   506	                                  "Copy the template, edit the values, then re-run "
   507	                                  "'run_mode.py apply'. A run never starts with an "
   508	                                  "assumed capacity.")
   509	    raw = path.read_bytes()
   510	    digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
   511	    try:
   512	        doc = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
   513	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   514	        raise BriefError("brief", f"{path} is not valid JSON: {exc}\n{_template_hint()}") from exc
   515	    return validate_brief(doc), digest

   522	def measured_limits(root: Path | None = None, names: list[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   523	    """Per-account `measured_limit` from the capacity controller, if any.
   524	
   525	    An unreadable or malformed estimate degrades to "no measurement" with a
   526	    warning: a corrupt runtime file must never become zero capacity.
   527	    """
   528	    base = root or cache_root()
   529	    path = base / "watchdog" / "capacity" / "limit-estimate.json"
   530	    if not path.exists():
   531	        return {}
   532	    try:
   533	        doc = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   534	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   535	        sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: warning: ignoring {path}: {exc}\n")
   536	        return {}
   537	    accounts = doc.get("accounts") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
   538	    source = accounts if isinstance(accounts, dict) else doc if isinstance(doc, dict) else {}
   539	    out: dict[str, int] = {}
   540	    for name in (names if names is not None else list(source)):
   541	        row = source.get(name)
   542	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   543	            continue
   544	        value = row.get("measured_limit")
   545	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
   546	            continue
   547	        out[name] = value
   548	    return out

   551	def effective_caps(brief: dict, measured: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   552	    """Starting cap per account.
   553	
   554	    ``cap0 = clamp(1, nominal_limit - external_reserved,
   555	    last_measured_limit or nominal_limit - external_reserved)`` — a run starts
   556	    below the measured cliff instead of above it.  A disabled or unlisted
   557	    account is 0: the pipeline never dispatches there at all.
   558	    """
   559	    seen = measured or {}
   560	    caps = {account["name"]: 0 for account in brief["accounts"]}
   561	    for account in brief["accounts"]:
   562	        if not account["enabled"]:
   563	            continue
   564	        base = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   565	        target = base
   566	        limit = seen.get(account["name"])
   567	        if isinstance(limit, int) and limit >= 0:
   568	            target = min(base, limit)
   569	        # A live entry may reach ``ceiling == external_reserved``: the admin has
   570	        # taken every slot of that key for now.  That is 0, not the floor of 1 —
   571	        # the clamp exists so a measured limit never seeds a disabled-looking
   572	        # cap, not to invent a slot the owner says is not theirs.
   573	        caps[account["name"]] = max(1, min(base, target)) if base > 0 else 0
   574	    return caps

   759	
   760	    ``strict_accounts=False`` keeps an INVALID accounts file from taking the
   761	    caller down with it.  It is for commands that can only ever narrow capacity
   762	    or that touch no ceiling at all: `pause` zeroes every cap file it finds, so a
   763	    stale name list cannot widen anything, and `get owner_inbox_issue` is how the
   764	    owner's remote repair path finds the issue to repair the file from.  Before
   765	    this, one mistyped field in the file the owner is invited to hand-edit made
   766	    `run_mode.py pause` exit 2 — so `owner-pause.sh` failed at T+0:00, admission
   767	    was never stopped, the pre-pause caps were never saved — and took the GitHub
   768	    channel down with it, exactly when the file needed remote repair.

   770	    path = (root or cache_root()) / "watchdog" / "run-mode.json"

   773	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:

  1217	    """Re-render the operator crontab for the current run mode.
  1218

  1220	    mode file is a real change, so a missing or failing installer is a warning
  1221	    to act on rather than a reason to leave the run half-switched.

  1227	    if dry_run:
  1228	        return f"would regenerate the crontab through {path}"
  1229	    try:

  1231	    except OSError as exc:
  1232	        return f"crontab NOT regenerated: cannot run {path} ({exc}); run it by hand"
  1233	    if proc.returncode != 0:
  1234	        detail = (proc.stdout + proc.stderr).strip()[:400] or f"exit {proc.returncode}"

  1253	def seed_accounts(brief: dict, digest: str, source: Path, *,
  1254	                  dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
  1255	    """Write ``watchdog/accounts.json`` from the brief, only when it is absent.
  1256	
  1257	    The brief is ONE-SHOT and the accounts file is LIVE.  A brief re-applied
  1258	    mid-run — to change the speed tier, the cutoff or an issue number — must not
  1259	    undo an hour of the owner's ceiling edits, so an existing file is left
  1260	    exactly as it is and this says so.  The owner's own tools
  1261	    (``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, the ``ACCOUNTS:`` inbox comment) are the way
  1262	    it changes afterwards; ``rm`` it and re-apply to go back to the brief.
  1263	    """
  1264	    path = accounts_file.accounts_path()
  1265	    if path.exists():
  1266	        return f"{path} kept (the live accounts file is the owner's; the brief seeds it once)"
  1267	    if dry_run:
  1268	        return (f"{path} would be seeded from {source} with " +
  1269	                ", ".join(f"{a['name']}={a['nominal_limit']}" for a in brief["accounts"]))
  1270	    try:
  1271	        written, path = accounts_file.seed(
  1272	            brief["accounts"], source=f"seeded from {source} sha256 {digest[:12]}")
  1273	    except accounts_file.AccountsError as exc:
  1274	        raise BriefError("accounts", f"cannot seed {path}: {exc}") from exc

  1296	def cmd_apply(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
  1297	    source = Path(args.brief).expanduser() if args.brief else brief_path()
  1298	    brief, digest = read_brief(source)
  1299	    accounts_note = seed_accounts(brief, digest, source, dry_run=args.dry_run)
  1300	    brief = dict(brief, accounts=live_accounts(brief))
  1301	    names = names_of(brief)
  1302	    measured = measured_limits(names=names)
  1303	    caps = effective_caps(brief, measured)
  1304	    mode = build_mode(brief, digest, source, caps, measured)
  1305	    values = cap_values(caps)
  1306	    run = mode["run"]
  1307	    summary = (f"speed {run['speed']}, caps " +
  1308	               ", ".join(f"{name} {caps[name]}" for name in names) +
  1309	               f", max-codex {values['max-codex']}, occupancy floor "
  1310	               f"{mode['derived']['floor']} (target {run['occupancy_target']:.2f}), "
  1311	               f"cutoff {run['dispatch_cutoff']}, issues "
  1312	               f"progress #{run['progress_issue']} estimate #{run['estimate_issue']} "
  1313	               f"inbox #{run['owner_inbox_issue']}, override "
  1314	               f"{mode_override(mode)[0] or 'none'}, account mode "
  1315	               f"{account_mode(mode)}")
  1316	
  1317	    if args.dry_run:
  1318	        sys.stdout.write(render_show(mode))
  1319	        sys.stdout.write("\nwould write:\n")
  1320	        sys.stdout.write(f"  {mode_path()}\n")
  1321	        for name, value in values.items():
  1322	            sys.stdout.write(f"  {watchdog_dir() / name} = {value}\n")
  1323	        sys.stdout.write(f"  {shim_path()} rendered at {run['speed']} speed\n")
  1324	        sys.stdout.write(f"  {write_model_override(mode, dry_run=True)}\n")
  1325	        sys.stdout.write(f"  {write_account_mode(mode, dry_run=True)}\n")
  1326	        sys.stdout.write(f"  {accounts_note}\n")
  1327	        sys.stdout.write(f"  brief sha256 {digest}\n")
  1328	        return 0
  1329	
  1330	    previous_paused = False
  1331	    try:
  1332	        previous_paused = bool(load_mode().get("paused"))
  1333	    except LayerError:
  1334	        pass
  1335	    path = write_mode(mode)
  1336	    ok, detail = call_controller("init")
  1337	    if detail == "not installed":
  1338	        write_caps(caps)
  1339	    elif not ok:
  1340	        raise Refused(f"capacity_controller.py init failed: {detail}\n"
  1341	                      "The installed controller owns the cap files; fix it and re-run apply.")
  1342	    override_note = write_model_override(mode)
  1343	    account_mode_note = write_account_mode(mode)
  1344	    # Hand the briefed caps to the capacity controller, which is the sole writer
  1345	    # of watchdog/capacity/state.json and therefore the thing `pause` asks to
  1346	    # save them and `resume` asks to restore them.  Without this seed the
  1347	    # controller has no state, `pause` saves zeros, and `resume` restores the
  1348	    # floor: a briefed 5/28/33 came back as 1/1/2 while the resume message
  1349	    # announced 5/28/33 - the exact defect of the 2026-09-12 resume script.
  1350	    append_stage(f"run-mode apply: {summary}; {override_note}; {account_mode_note}; "
  1351	                 f"{accounts_note}; brief {source} sha256 {digest}", "run-mode-apply")
  1352	    append_decision(
  1353	        f"Run mode applied: {summary}",
  1354	        "owner brief via run_mode.py apply",
  1355	        "one briefing per run; capacity, schedule, speed and issue numbers live only in "
  1356	        "watchdog/run-brief.json and are read through run_mode.py get",
  1357	        f"brief sha256 {digest[:12]}; {path}; stages.jsonl event=run-mode-apply")
  1358	    sys.stdout.write(render_show(mode))
  1359	    sys.stdout.write(override_note + "\n")
  1360	    sys.stdout.write(account_mode_note + "\n")
  1361	    sys.stdout.write(accounts_note + "\n")
  1362	    if previous_paused:
  1363	        sys.stdout.write("note: the previous run mode was paused; this brief restores "
  1364	                         "capacity now.\n")
  1365	    # The briefed speed must reach the deployed shim, or `fast` is a word in a
  1366	    # file and every worker runs at default speed (2026-09-12, three hand
  1367	    # patches).  A missing or hand-edited shim is reported loudly and never
  1368	    # silently overwritten; the caps above are applied either way.

  1370	        sys.stdout.write(apply_speed(mode, run["speed"]) + "\n")
  1371	    except (Refused, LayerError) as exc:
  1372	        sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: warning: the shim was NOT regenerated: {exc}\n"
  1373	                         f"Fix it, then run 'run_mode.py set speed {run['speed']}'.\n")

  1093	retry_is_safe() {
  1094	  # A transient CLASS is not by itself a licence to re-run the prompt.
  1095	  # `refused`, `endpoint_down`, `concurrency_limit` and `endpoint_5xx` are
  1096	  # admission failures: the model never ran, the worktree was never touched, and
  1097	  # a retry is a pure re-attempt.  `retries_exhausted` is different — the client
  1098	  # gave up reconnecting, which can happen twenty minutes in, and re-running the
  1099	  # same prompt from scratch in a worktree that now holds the dead session's
  1100	  # partial, uncommitted edits is not a retry, it is a second worker on a dirty
  1101	  # tree.  review.sh already draws this line (ended-started < 15 s, tokens 0);
  1102	  # draw the same one here: retry only a death that did no work and left a clean
  1103	  # tree.  Anything else is left to the janitor's dead-session pass, which
  1104	  # re-dispatches under a per-(pr, role, head) budget with the state in hand.

  1106	  if [ "${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}" != "${WORKTREE_STATUS_BEFORE_CODEX:-}" ]; then

  1112	    ''|0) ;;

  1114	before dying, so a re-run would repeat work in a tree that holds its partial edits"

  1116	  esac

  1118	    note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': $WORKTREE_ABS has uncommitted changes from the \
  1119	dead session; the janitor's dead-session pass owns this one"

  1121	  fi
  1122	  return 0
  1123	}

  1129	    note "attempt $ATTEMPT of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; no attempt left"
  1130	    return 1
  1131	  fi

  1133	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff has passed; not retrying after '$FAILURE_CLASS'"
  1134	    return 1
  1135	  fi
  1136	  exponent=$((ATTEMPT - 1))
  1137	  [ "$exponent" -le 20 ] || exponent=20
  1138	  delay=$((BACKOFF_BASE_S * (1 << exponent)))
  1139	  [ "$delay" -le "$BACKOFF_MAX_S" ] || delay="$BACKOFF_MAX_S"

item.text: The core repair paths now fail closed as intended, and the eleven prior findings are mostly resolved. Two behavioral edges need deeper checking: zero-share enabled accounts are explicitly legal but the resume wrapper still treats cap 0 as failure, and retry safety compares only porcelain status labels rather than file content.

  1093	retry_is_safe() {
  1094	  # A transient CLASS is not by itself a licence to re-run the prompt.
  1095	  # `refused`, `endpoint_down`, `concurrency_limit` and `endpoint_5xx` are
  1096	  # admission failures: the model never ran, the worktree was never touched, and
  1097	  # a retry is a pure re-attempt.  `retries_exhausted` is different — the client
  1098	  # gave up reconnecting, which can happen twenty minutes in, and re-running the
  1099	  # same prompt from scratch in a worktree that now holds the dead session's
  1100	  # partial, uncommitted edits is not a retry, it is a second worker on a dirty
  1101	  # tree.  review.sh already draws this line (ended-started < 15 s, tokens 0);
  1102	  # draw the same one here: retry only a death that did no work and left a clean
  1103	  # tree.  Anything else is left to the janitor's dead-session pass, which
  1104	  # re-dispatches under a per-(pr, role, head) budget with the state in hand.
  1105	  local dirty=""
  1106	  if [ "${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}" != "${WORKTREE_STATUS_BEFORE_CODEX:-}" ]; then
  1107	    dirty="${WORKTREE_STATUS_AFTER_CODEX:-}"
  1108	  fi
  1109	  [ "${DISPATCH_STATUS:-}" = refused ] || return 1
  1110	  [ "${DISPATCH_TURNS:-0}" = 0 ] || return 1
  1111	  case "${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL:-0}" in
  1112	    ''|0) ;;
  1113	    *) note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': the session used ${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL} tokens \
  1114	before dying, so a re-run would repeat work in a tree that holds its partial edits"
  1115	       return 1 ;;
  1116	  esac
  1117	  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
  1118	    note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': $WORKTREE_ABS has uncommitted changes from the \
  1119	dead session; the janitor's dead-session pass owns this one"
  1120	    return 1
  1121	  fi
  1122	  return 0
  1123	}

  1125	backoff_or_give_up() {
  1126	  # Jittered exponential backoff, base 30 s and cap 10 min. Returns 0 to retry.
  1127	  local exponent delay jitter total
  1128	  if [ "$ATTEMPT" -ge "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
  1129	    note "attempt $ATTEMPT of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; no attempt left"
  1130	    return 1
  1131	  fi
  1132	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1133	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff has passed; not retrying after '$FAILURE_CLASS'"
  1134	    return 1
  1135	  fi
  1136	  exponent=$((ATTEMPT - 1))
  1137	  [ "$exponent" -le 20 ] || exponent=20
  1138	  delay=$((BACKOFF_BASE_S * (1 << exponent)))
  1139	  [ "$delay" -le "$BACKOFF_MAX_S" ] || delay="$BACKOFF_MAX_S"
  1140	  jitter=$((RANDOM % (delay / 2 + 1)))
  1141	  total=$((delay + jitter))
  1142	  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT + 1))
  1143	  write_spool retrying
  1144	  note "attempt $((ATTEMPT - 1)) of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; \
  1145	retrying as attempt $ATTEMPT in ${total}s"
  1146	  sleep "$total"
  1147	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1148	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff passed during the backoff; stopping"
  1149	    return 1
  1150	  fi
  1151	  return 0
  1152	}

  1154	report_and_exit_refused() {
  1155	  # One `refused` row for the whole episode, then exit 7 with the spool intact.
  1156	  # `refused` is not `failed`: the dispatch was never admitted, so it must not
  1157	  # be scored as a failed attempt against a proof packet's budget.
  1158	  local ts

  1160	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then

  1162	\"attempts\":$ATTEMPT,\"account\":\"$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED\",\"endpoint\":\"$ENDPOINT_LABEL\",\
  1163	\"ts\":\"$ts\"}" >"$CAPTURE"

  1165	      note "warning: could not copy the refusal record into $PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR"

  1169	      --status refused --failure-class "$FAILURE_CLASS" --key-label "$KEY_LABEL"

  1185	}

   908	    if key == "accounts":
   909	        return " ".join(a["name"] for a in mode["accounts"] if a.get("enabled"))

   912	        if field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS and name in names_of(mode):

   922	                   [f"{field}.<account>" for field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS])
   923	    raise LayerError(f"unknown key {key!r}; known keys: {', '.join(known)}")

  1029	    # the template's header documents both renderings, and a comment that merely

  1031	    speed_lines = _SPEED_ARGS_RE.findall(template)

  1036	                "with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required (install.sh renders "

  1038	        return _SPEED_ARGS_RE.sub(
  1039	            lambda _match: SPEED_ARGS_LINE[speed], template, count=1)

  1042	        return _PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(PRIORITY_ARG + " " if speed == "fast" else "", stripped)

  1047	            "committed template (results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex) rather "
  1048	            "than hand-patching the deployed shim.")

  1054	def record_shim() -> str:
  1055	    """Re-record the regenerated shim in ``owner-bin/manifest.sha256``.
  1056	
  1057	    ``install.sh`` releases both renderings into ``manifest.accepted`` but keeps
  1058	    ``manifest.sha256`` at the deployed one, and the merge daemon's start gate is
  1059	    ``install.sh --verify``.  Without this step the first ``set speed`` of a run
  1060	    makes the daemon refuse to start.  Best effort: a missing or failing
  1061	    installer is a warning, never a reason to leave the speed change unmade.
  1062	    """
  1063	    installer = repo_root() / "results" / "telemetry" / "owner-tools" / "install.sh"
  1064	    if not installer.is_file():
  1065	        return f"manifest not re-recorded: no {installer}"
  1066	    try:
  1067	        done = subprocess.run(["bash", str(installer), "--record", "codex"],
  1068	                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
  1069	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
  1070	        return f"warning: install.sh --record codex did not run: {exc}"
  1071	    if done.returncode != 0:
  1072	        detail = (done.stderr or done.stdout).strip().splitlines()
  1073	        return ("warning: install.sh --record codex failed: "
  1074	                + (detail[-1] if detail else f"exit {done.returncode}"))
  1075	    return "manifest re-recorded (install.sh --record codex)"

    96	def readiness(pull: dict, statuses: dict, reviews: list[dict]) -> dict:
    97	    """Readiness of one PR on its exact head, with the blockers named."""
    98	    head = ((pull.get("head") or {}).get("sha")) or ""
    99	    number = int(pull["number"])
   100	    branch = (pull.get("head") or {}).get("ref") or ""
   101	    ci = (statuses.get("local-ci/summary") or {}).get("state")
   102	    review = (statuses.get("local-review/summary") or {}).get("state")
   103	    head_reviews = [row for row in reviews if row.get("commit_id") == head]
   104	    marked = [row for row in head_reviews if REVIEW_MARKER in (row.get("body") or "")]
   105	    unchecked = (len(UNCHECKED_RE.findall(marked[-1].get("body") or ""))
   106	                 if marked else None)
   107	    adverse = any(row.get("state") == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" for row in head_reviews)
   108	
   109	    blockers: list[str] = []
   110	    if pull.get("draft"):
   111	        blockers.append("draft")
   112	    if ci != "success":
   113	        blockers.append(f"ci={ci or 'absent'}")
   114	    if review != "success":
   115	        blockers.append(f"review={review or 'absent'}")
   116	    if unchecked is None:
   117	        blockers.append("no exact-head review")
   118	    elif unchecked:
   119	        blockers.append(f"{unchecked} unchecked findings")
   120	    if adverse:
   121	        blockers.append("CHANGES_REQUESTED")
   122	    return {
   123	        "pr": number,
   124	        "head": head,
   125	        "branch": branch,
   126	        "issue": issue_of(branch),
   127	        "ready": not blockers,
   128	        "blockers": blockers,
   129	        "unchecked": unchecked,
   130	    }

   149	def _minutes_since(path: Path, now: datetime) -> int | None:
   150	    try:
   151	        stamp = datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime, tz=timezone.utc)
   152	    except OSError:
   153	        return None
   154	    return max(0, int((now - stamp).total_seconds() // 60))

   157	def read_marker(path: Path) -> dict | None:
   158	    """The daemon's failure marker: JSON record, or the legacy touch file."""
   159	    try:
   160	        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
   161	    except OSError:
   162	        return None
   163	    if not text:
   164	        return {"class": "legacy", "reason": "empty marker (pre-W5 touch file)"}
   165	    try:
   166	        record = json.loads(text)
   167	    except ValueError:
   168	        return {"class": "legacy", "reason": text.splitlines()[0][:120]}
   169	    if not isinstance(record, dict):

   174	def classify_reason(row: dict, *, daemon_dir: Path, lanes_dir: Path,
   175	                    fresh: bool | None, base_moved_min: int | None,
   176	                    adjudicating: bool, now: datetime) -> dict:
   177	    """One (class, detail, key) for a ready-but-open PR.
   178	
   179	    ``key`` is the suppression-stable part: it carries no elapsed timer, so an
   180	    unchanged situation produces an unchanged signature an hour later.
   181	    """
   182	    number, head = row["pr"], row["head"]
   183	    refreshing = daemon_dir / f"pr{number}.refreshing"
   184	    if refreshing.exists():
   185	        try:
   186	            pid = int(refreshing.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip() or 0)
   187	        except (OSError, ValueError):
   188	            pid = 0
   189	        if pid and pid_alive(pid):
   190	            elapsed = _minutes_since(refreshing, now)
   191	            lane = row.get("issue")
   192	            return {"class": "refreshing", "key": "refreshing",
   193	                    "detail": f"refreshing pid {pid} lane {lane}, "
   194	                              f"{elapsed if elapsed is not None else '?'} min"}
   195	
   196	    marker = daemon_dir / f"pr{number}.failed"
   197	    if marker.exists():
   198	        record = read_marker(marker) or {}
   199	        kind = str(record.get("class") or "unknown")
   200	        reason = str(record.get("reason") or "no reason recorded")[:160]
   201	        attempts = record.get("attempts")
   202	        marked_head = str(record.get("head") or "")
   203	        stale_marker = (" (marker on a different head " f"{marked_head[:8]})"
   204	                        if marked_head and marked_head != head else "")
   205	        detail = (f"failed marker class={kind} reason={reason!r}"
   206	                  + (f" attempts={attempts}" if attempts is not None else "")
   207	                  + stale_marker)
   208	        return {"class": "failed", "key": f"failed:{kind}:{reason}{stale_marker}",
   209	                "detail": detail}
   210	
   211	    lane = row.get("issue")
   212	    if lane is not None:
   213	        parked = lanes_dir / f"{lane}.needs-attention"
   214	        if parked.exists():
   215	            try:
   216	                reason = parked.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip().splitlines()
   217	            except OSError:
   218	                reason = []
   219	            text = (reason[0] if reason else "no reason recorded")[:160]
   220	            return {"class": "parked", "key": f"parked:{text}",
   221	                    "detail": f"lane {lane} parked: {text}"}
   222	
   223	    if adjudicating:
   224	        return {"class": "awaiting-adjudication", "key": "awaiting-adjudication",
   225	                "detail": "on the daemon adjudication list, no exact-head "
   226	                          "ADJUDICATION comment yet"}
   227	
   228	    if fresh is False:
   229	        since = f"{base_moved_min} min ago" if base_moved_min is not None else "recently"
   230	        return {"class": "stale", "key": "stale",
   231	                "detail": f"stale: main moved {since}; needs a refresh lane"}
   232	    if fresh is None:
   233	        return {"class": "unknown-freshness", "key": "unknown-freshness",
   234	                "detail": "freshness could not be read locally (git failure)"}
   235	
   236	    return {"class": "unexplained", "key": "unexplained",
   237	            "detail": "ready, fresh, and no daemon record — investigate"}

   283	    status`` on the host — so "the yxy key is disabled and here is why" reached
   284	    the owner as a message from a session, which is exactly the prompt the live
   285	    accounts file exists to remove.  Every field comes from the component that
   286	    owns it: the ceiling and the note from ``watchdog/accounts.json`` (the
   287	    owner's own file, so the line echoes back what they last wrote), the cap
