   353	def refusals_by_account(repo_root: Path, entries: list[dict],
   354	                        since: datetime) -> dict[str, int]:
   355	    """Refusals per account since *since*, classified by the capacity policy.
   356	
   357	    The policy is the single place that says which ``failure_class`` counts as a
   358	    refusal, so this cannot drift from what the controller's AIMD reacted to.
   359	    An unreadable policy degrades to the two classes every generation of the
   360	    pipeline has used, never to "no refusals" — a silent zero here would read as
   361	    a healthy key.
   362	    """
   363	    try:
   364	        import capacity_controller  # noqa: PLC0415 - same directory
   365	        roles = capacity_controller.class_roles(capacity_controller.load_policy())
   366	        refusal_classes = {name for name, role in roles.items() if role == "refusal"}
   367	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
   368	        refusal_classes = {"concurrency_limit", "refused"}
   369	    # The same attribution the controller's AIMD used, for the same reason: an
   370	    # endpoint shared by two keys (the owner's own topology) names neither of
   371	    # them, so a token more than one entry claims is dropped instead of resolved
   372	    # to whichever entry wrote it last, and the row's own `account` is read
   373	    # first.  Reporting the collapse back to the owner as a per-key number was
   374	    # how the wrong key looked guilty in their hourly line as well.
   375	    owner: dict[str, str] = {entry["name"]: entry["name"] for entry in entries}
   376	    claimed: dict[str, str] = {}
   377	    ambiguous: set[str] = set()
   378	    for entry in entries:
   379	        for key in (entry.get("endpoint"), entry.get("label")):
   380	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key or key in owner:
   381	                continue
   382	            if claimed.setdefault(key, entry["name"]) != entry["name"]:
   383	                ambiguous.add(key)
   384	    owner.update({key: name for key, name in claimed.items() if key not in ambiguous})
   385	    counts: dict[str, int] = {entry["name"]: 0 for entry in entries}
   386	    path = repo_root / "results" / "telemetry" / "sessions.jsonl"
   387	    for row in _rows_in_window(path, since, ("end", "start", "ts")):
   388	        if row.get("failure_class") not in refusal_classes:
   389	            continue
   390	        recorded_account = row.get("account")
   391	        if (isinstance(recorded_account, str)
   392	                and accounts_file.NAME_RE.match(recorded_account)):
   393	            name = recorded_account if recorded_account in counts else None
   394	        else:
   395	            name = next((owner[row[field]] for field in
   396	                         ("endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "key_label")
   397	                         if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in owner), None)
   398	        if name is not None:
   399	            counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
   400	    return counts

   403	def _rows_in_window(path: Path, since: datetime,
   404	                    field: str | tuple[str, ...]) -> list[dict]:
   405	    """JSONL rows whose *field* parses as a timestamp at or after *since*.
   406	
   407	    A tuple takes the FIRST field that parses, so one pass over a registry whose
   408	    rows carry ``end`` or only ``start`` yields each row exactly once; reading
   409	    the file twice and concatenating would count a completed row twice.
   410	    """
   411	    fields = (field,) if isinstance(field, str) else field
   412	    out: list[dict] = []
   413	    try:
   414	        handle = path.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   415	    except OSError:
   416	        return out
   417	    with handle:
   418	        for line in handle:
   419	            line = line.strip()
   420	            if not line:
   421	                continue
   422	            try:
   423	                row = json.loads(line)
   424	            except ValueError:
   425	                continue
   426	            if not isinstance(row, dict):
   427	                continue
   428	            moment = None
   429	            for candidate in fields:
   430	                try:
   431	                    moment = run_mode.parse_timestamp(row.get(candidate), candidate)
   432	                    break
   433	                except LayerError:
   434	                    continue
   435	            if moment is not None and moment >= since:
   436	                out.append(row)
   437	    return out

   440	def model_census(repo_root: Path, since: datetime) -> dict | None:
   441	    """Sessions started since *since*, grouped by the model that actually ran.
   442	
   443	    Follow-up item W9(5): *"a check in the janitor or the daily digest that
   444	    counts sessions per resolved model so a wrong model shows up within an
   445	    hour"*.  Without it the only way to confirm that a fast run really put every
   446	    role — reviewers included — on the hard model was to read sessions.jsonl by
   447	    hand, which is exactly the owner audit the override exists to remove.
   448	
   449	    ``model`` on a session row is the RESOLVED model (``dispatch.sh`` records
   450	    what it asked ``model_policy.py`` for and what ran).  The expectation comes
   450	    what it asked ``model_policy.py`` for and what ran).  The expectation comes
   451	    from the run mode's effective ``model_override``: ``astra-all`` means every
   452	    row should read ``gpt-6-astra``.  With no override in force there is no
   453	    single expected model and ``off_policy`` is 0 — the census still reports the
   454	    split, which is the number the ratio is argued from.
   455	    """
   456	    path = repo_root / "results" / "telemetry" / "sessions.jsonl"
   457	    try:
   458	        override = str(run_mode.value_for(
   459	            run_mode.load_mode(strict_accounts=False), "model_override"))
   460	    except (LayerError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
   461	        override = "unknown"
   462	    try:
   463	        import model_policy  # noqa: PLC0415 - same directory, optional
   464	        expected = model_policy.ASTRA if override == "astra-all" else None
   465	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - a policy import failure must not lose the report
   466	        expected = "gpt-6-astra" if override == "astra-all" else None
   467	
   468	    by_model: dict[str, int] = {}
   469	    for row in _rows_in_window(path, since, "start"):
   470	        name = str(row.get("model") or "unrecorded")
   471	        by_model[name] = by_model.get(name, 0) + 1
   472	    total = sum(by_model.values())
   473	    if not total:
   474	        return {"override": override, "expected": expected, "by_model": {},
   475	                "total": 0, "off_policy": 0}
   476	    off = 0 if expected is None else sum(
   477	        count for name, count in by_model.items() if name != expected)
   478	    return {"override": override, "expected": expected, "by_model": by_model,
   479	            "total": total, "off_policy": off}

   512	def render_key_line(row: dict) -> str:
   513	    """One key's line: what it may use, what it is using, and whether it works."""
   514	    # An absent cap file is what `account_router.effective_caps` reads as a hard
   515	    # 0 — the state of a key added between two ticks.  "unknown" read to the
   516	    # owner as a reporting glitch rather than as "not admitted yet".
   517	    cap = "0 (no cap file yet)" if row["cap"] is None else row["cap"]
   518	    state = row["health"] if row["enabled"] else f"{row['health']}/off"
   519	    line = (f"- key {row['name']} ({row['label']}, {row['endpoint']}): ceiling "
   520	            f"{row['ceiling']}" +
   521	            (f" less {row['reserved']} reserved" if row["reserved"] else "") +
   522	            f", cap {cap}, live {row['live']}, refusals/{KEY_REFUSAL_WINDOW_MIN}m "
   523	            f"{row['refusals']}, health {state}")
   524	    if row["reason"]:
   525	        line += f" ({row['reason']})"
   526	    if not row["enabled"]:

   528	    elif row["health"] == "down":

   542	    if occ is not None:
   543	        detail = ", ".join(f"{name} {count}" for name, count in sorted(occ["by_account"].items()))

   547	    for key in keys or []:

   584	def signature(rows: list[dict], occ: dict | None = None,
   585	              keys: list[dict] | None = None, models: dict | None = None,
   586	              dead: dict | None = None) -> str:
   587	    """Stable digest of the ready set and its reasons (no elapsed timers).
   588	
   589	    The occupancy ALARM state joins it — not the live count, which changes every
   590	    minute and would defeat the suppression — so that crossing the floor in
   591	    either direction posts instead of being suppressed as "unchanged".
   592	    """
   593	    ready_keys = sorted(f"{row['pr']}:{row['head']}:{row['reason']['key']}"
   594	                        for row in rows if row["ready"])
   595	    payload = f"ready={len(ready_keys)}\n" + "\n".join(ready_keys)
   596	    if occ is not None:
   597	        payload += f"\noccupancy_below={int(bool(occ['below']))}"
   598	    # A key's ceiling, cap, health or enabled flag changing is exactly the event
   599	    # the owner wants the next hourly comment to carry, so it joins the
   600	    # signature; `live` and `refusals` do not, or nothing would ever suppress.
   601	    for key in keys or []:
   602	        payload += (f"\nkey={key['name']}:{key['ceiling']}:{key['reserved']}:"
   603	                    f"{key['cap']}:{key['health']}:{int(bool(key['enabled']))}")
   604	    if models is not None:
   605	        payload += f"\noff_policy_models={int(models.get('off_policy', 0))}"
   606	    if dead is not None:
   607	        payload += "\ndead=" + ",".join(
   608	            f"{role}:{count}" for role, count in sorted(dead.get("by_role", {}).items()))
   609	    return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

   757	def collect(repo_root: Path, cache: Path, now: datetime) -> list[dict]:
   758	    """Every open PR with its readiness and, when ready, its reason."""
   759	    daemon_dir = cache / "watchdog" / "daemon"

   765	        head = ((pull.get("head") or {}).get("sha")) or ""

   768	        statuses = gh_common.latest_statuses(head)
   769	        reviews = gh_common.pr_reviews(int(pull["number"]))
   770	        row = readiness(pull, statuses, reviews)
   771	        if row["ready"]:

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# Usage: local/bin/janitor.sh [--dry-run] [--pass NAME]... [--list-passes]
     4	#                             [--no-lock] [--report PATH] [--help]
     5	#
     6	# The self-repair pass.  ONE idempotent sweep, safe to run from cron or from the
     7	# merge daemon's loop, that turns every terminal state the pipeline can reach
     8	# into either a repair or a reported line.  Everything it does is selected by a
     9	# record field — a session status, a marker's reason string, a PR state, a spool
    10	# deadline — and never by a date glob or a filename digit filter.  The
    11	# 2026-09-12 recovery script globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and matched
    12	# `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$` with `-mmin -15`, so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx
    13	# lanes were never repaired and a marker missed by one poll was never picked up
    14	# again.  Nothing here has an age filter or a digit-count filter.
    15	#
    16	# The five passes, each independently guarded (one failing pass never aborts the
    17	# others; a GitHub error is reported and retried next pass, never converted into
    18	# a local success):
    19	#
    20	#   dead-sessions   results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl rows whose last status is
    21	#                   `active` and whose process is gone.  When the capture ends in
    22	#                   an exhausted reconnect, a 5xx or a concurrency refusal the
    23	#                   same role is re-dispatched on the same PR and the same head,
    24	#                   at most twice per (pr, role, head_sha), ledger
    25	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl.  A capture that
    26	#                   ends cleanly is NEVER re-dispatched.  The abandoned row is
    27	#                   marked `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live.
    28	#                   This is the recovery path for the 25 reviews that were re-run
    29	#                   by hand after the 503 outage: review.sh retries only a
    30	#                   pre-model death (ended-started < 15 s and tokens 0), so a
    31	#                   reviewer that dies after twenty minutes at
    32	#                   "Reconnecting... 5/5" leaves the PR pending forever.
    33	#                   SCOPE: only a role with a re-dispatch entry point is
    34	#                   re-dispatched, and today that is `reviewer` alone
    35	#                   (review.sh, exact head, verdict supersedes).  A dead prover,
    36	#                   orc or fixer is marked `failed` with a `residue` field in
    37	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl and is the owning
    38	#                   session's to re-plan; `local/bin/ready_report.py` counts
    39	#                   those rows PER ROLE into the hourly comment on the progress
    40	#                   issue, so the unrepaired remainder reaches the owner's
    41	#                   channel instead of a local log.
    42	#   parked-lanes    every $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention, no digit
    43	#                   filter and no age filter.  The recorded reason is classified;
    44	#                   `merge` and `build` go to fix-lane.sh with the committed
    45	#                   brief, at most twice per lane; every other class stays parked
    46	#                   and appears in the report.
    47	#   superseded-prs  local/bin/pr_janitor.py (empty three-dot diff AND head
    48	#                   reachable from github/main; one idempotent marker comment;
    49	#                   never closes an issue).
    50	#   stale-lanes     lane state for lanes whose PR is closed or merged is deleted
    51	#                   (20 stale 1xxx lanes were left behind on 2026-09-12).
    52	#   spool-expiry    $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json entries past the
    53	#                   run's dispatch_cutoff are dropped, so a spool that outlives a
    54	#                   run cannot re-launch stale work.
    55	#   owner-accounts  `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]
    56	#                   [enabled=true|false]` comments on the owner inbox issue are
    57	#                   applied to the live accounts file and answered with one
    58	#                   `applied:` / `rejected:` reply per comment
    59	#                   (local/bin/accounts_inbox.py).  ONLY comments written by the
    60	#                   repository owner login are applied; the author check, the
    61	#                   parsing and the validation live in that tool and in
    62	#                   local/bin/accounts_file.py, never here.  It is the owner's
    63	#                   channel for a ceiling change when they are away from a
    64	#                   shell: on 2026-09-12 every such change was a message to a
    65	#                   session that had to be idle to receive it.
    66	#
    67	# The janitor repairs; it never merges, never pushes, never closes an issue and
    68	# never touches a gate.  Repairs are dispatched through fix-lane.sh ->
    69	# dispatch.sh (agents never invoke codex directly) and the lane tail is
    70	# relaunched through the repository's own local/bin/lane.sh.
    71	#
    72	# Runner: results/telemetry/owner-tools/merge-daemon.sh calls this once every
    73	# `janitor_interval_s` (daemon.conf), detached and bounded; the sweep takes its
    74	# own lock, so an overlapping call exits instead of doubling up.  Nothing else
    75	# runs it: a checkout whose merge daemon is not running has no self-repair.
    76	#
    77	# Output: one line per action on stdout, the same lines in
    78	# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/report.md (the operator's log of the sweep; the
    79	# hourly readiness report does NOT read it — it reports merges and readiness
    80	# from daemon state) and one append-only JSONL row per action in
    81	# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/{retries,repairs,actions,closures}.jsonl.
    82	#
    83	# Exit codes: 0 all passes completed; 1 at least one pass failed (the others
    84	# still ran); 2 usage/environment error.
    85	#
    86	# Environment:
    87	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT             override ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev
    88	#   MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT              override the checkout (default: this file's)
    89	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP      re-dispatches per (pr, role, head)  [2]
    90	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP     repairs per lane                    [2]
    91	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S        a dead session's capture must be this old
    92	#                                    before it is judged abandoned       [900]
    93	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S    lane state younger than this is never
    94	#                                    deleted                             [3600]
    95	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES  roles the janitor may re-dispatch
    96	#                                    automatically; only a role with an entry
    97	#                                    point below may be listed    [reviewer]

   235	# capture_class FILE -> how a captured `codex exec --json` stream ended.
   236	#   clean               a completed turn is the last event   -> never re-dispatch
   237	#   reconnect-exhausted "Reconnecting... N/N" (the retry budget ran out)
   238	#   endpoint-5xx        503/502/500 from the endpoint
   239	#   concurrency-limit   the provider refused the session (concurrency / 429)
   240	#   empty               no capture, or an empty one
   241	#   unknown             anything else -> reported, never re-dispatched
   242	capture_class_builtin() {
   243	  local file="$1" last=""
   244	  [ -n "$file" ] && [ -s "$file" ] || { echo "empty"; return 0; }
   245	  last="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*$' "$file" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"
   246	  # A clean end wins over anything earlier in the stream: a session that
   247	  # reconnected once and then finished its turn is not a failure.
   248	  case "$last" in
   249	    *'"type":"turn.completed"'*|*'"type": "turn.completed"'*|\
   250	    *'"type":"thread.completed"'*|*'"type": "thread.completed"'*|\
   251	    *'"type":"session.completed"'*|*'"type": "session.completed"'*|\
   252	    *'"type":"response.completed"'*|*'"type": "response.completed"'*)
   253	      echo "clean"; return 0 ;;
   254	  esac
   255	  if grep -qE 'Reconnecting\.\.\.? ([0-9]+)/\1' "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
   256	    echo "reconnect-exhausted"; return 0
   257	  fi
   258	  if grep -qE '50[0-9] (Service Unavailable|Bad Gateway|Internal Server Error)|HTTP 5[0-9][0-9]|"status": ?5[0-9][0-9]' "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
   259	    echo "endpoint-5xx"; return 0
   260	  fi
   261	  if grep -qiE 'concurrency limit|too many requests|429|rate.?limit' "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
   262	    echo "concurrency-limit"; return 0
   263	  fi
   264	  echo "unknown"
   265	}

   328	# spool_is_expired FILE CUTOFF_ISO -> exit 0 when the entry may not be launched.
   329	# An entry is expired when its own deadline has passed or when the run's
   330	# dispatch_cutoff has.  An unparsable entry is NOT expired (it is reported).
   331	spool_is_expired() {
   332	  JAN_FILE="$1" JAN_CUTOFF="${2:-}" python3 - <<'PY'
   333	import json, os, sys, time
   334	from datetime import datetime, timezone
   335	
   336	def parse(value):
   337	    if not value:
   338	        return None
   339	    text = str(value).strip().replace("Z", "+00:00")
   340	    try:
   341	        stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
   342	    except ValueError:
   343	        return None
   344	    return stamp if stamp.tzinfo else stamp.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   345	
   346	try:
   347	    entry = json.load(open(os.environ["JAN_FILE"], encoding="utf-8"))
   348	except Exception:
   349	    sys.exit(1)
   350	now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   351	cutoff = parse(os.environ.get("JAN_CUTOFF"))
   352	deadline = entry.get("deadline_epoch") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None
   353	deadline_passed = isinstance(deadline, (int, float)) and deadline <= time.time()

     2	"""daemon-scan.py — the merge daemon's Python helper (promoted from /tmp, 2026-09-12).
     3	
     4	Historically this file held only the candidate scan.  It now also owns every
     5	*record format* the daemon reads and writes, so that the formats have one
     6	writer, one reader and a unit test instead of being re-derived by `grep` in
     7	bash (full-speed-mode v2 design §3.2-§3.5, work item W5).

     9	Subcommands
    10	    scan           one GraphQL call -> one line per open PR:
    11	                   ``PR:N:BRANCH:SLUG:MODE:HEAD`` with MODE in
    12	                   clean | adj | retire | offconv | skip.  Without ``--all``
    13	                   only clean/adj/retire lines are printed, which is the
    14	                   historical output plus the retirement pass.
    15	    classify       classify a lane / merge log into one of the six failure
    16	                   classes, printing ``CLASS<TAB>REASON``.
    17	    marker-write   write (or refresh) a classed failure marker, the JSON
    18	                   record that replaced ``touch pr<N>.failed``.
    19	    marker-check   decide whether a marker still blocks its PR.  Exit 0 =
    20	                   blocked, 10 = clear, 2 = usage.
    21	    marker-list    one line per live marker, for the hourly report; with
    22	                   ``--json-out`` also the machine-readable snapshot that
    23	                   ready_report.py reads instead of guessing a reason.
    24	    latency        append one ``merge-latency`` row.
    25	    par            the adaptive parallelism formula, with its inputs.
    26	    slots          free worker slots, read through local/bin/account_router.py.
    27	
    28	The marker record is::
    29	
    30	    {"pr": 342, "head": "<sha>", "ts": 1757650000, "class": "build",
    31	     "reason": "lake build before push failed (see ...)", "attempts": 2,
    32	     "lane_log": "/.../342.lane.log", "tools_version": "v9-g1a2b3c4",
    33	     "tools_ts": 1757649000}

    36	never on elapsed time alone -- except for the two classes whose backoff *is*
    37	the documented retry (infra 5 min, preflight 15 min):
    38	
    39	    class         blocked until
    40	    ------------  --------------------------------------------------------
    41	    conflict      the repair finishes (or the head changes)

    43	                  installed tools-version supersedes the marker

    46	                  head changes
    47	    gate          the head changes
    48	    adjudication  the head changes

    51	stayed blocked by 2 h markers after the systemic lane bugs had been fixed, and
    52	were freed by hand with ``rm`` and with ``( sleep 1500; rm -f ... )``.

     1	# Operator tools
     2	
     3	Scripts that drive tmux, the crontab and the host process table. They cannot be run from
     4	the checkout, because the checkout is mid-merge for minutes at a time, so they are
     5	**deployed** to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/` by one versioned installer and are
     6	**never edited on the host**. The file in this directory is the source of truth; the copy
     7	under `owner-bin/` is a build output with a recorded hash.
     8	
     9	On 2026-09-12 the same scripts lived in `/tmp` under names that no longer described their
    10	contents (`lane-v17.sh` was really v20), were patched in place by `assert anchor in src`
    11	here-docs, and ran in three simultaneous versions. That is what the installer exists to
    12	prevent.
    13	
    14	## Install
    15	
    16	```sh
    17	results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh --compat-tmp --crons --start-loops
    18	```
    19	
    20	`--start-loops` is not optional in practice: it starts `capacityd.sh`, and without a
    21	running controller nothing writes `watchdog/max-codex-*` again — no AIMD, no 5xx trip,
    22	no half-open probe, and on a fresh host no cap files at all, which makes
    23	`lane.sh:wait_for_slot` fail closed with `no-capacity-record`. The full run-start
    24	sequence is in `local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` §2.
    25	
    26	| Flag | Effect |
    27	|---|---|
    28	| *(none)* | copy every tool into `owner-bin/`, write `tools-version`, `manifest.sha256`, `manifest.accepted` and `repo-root` |
    29	| `--force` | overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version; the previous copy is **moved** to `owner-bin/attic/<ts>/`, never deleted |
    30	| `--compat-tmp` | create `/tmp/<name>` **symlinks** into `owner-bin/` for every historical name the 2026-09-12 run used, so an old invocation runs versioned code. A regular file in `/tmp` is left alone, not clobbered |
    31	| `--crons` | run `install-crons.sh` afterwards |
    32	| `--start-loops` | start `capacityd.sh` (the 60 s capacity controller) unless it is already running or `watchdog/capacity/capacityd.stop` holds it. The merge daemon and the keeper are not started here — `owner-resume.sh` owns those |
    33	| `--dry-run` | print the plan; touch nothing |
    34	| `--verify` | check every deployed file against `manifest.sha256`; exit 3 on a missing file or a mismatch. This is the merge daemon's start-up gate |
    35	| `--record <name>` | re-record one regenerated file's hash (`run_mode.py set speed` calls it for `codex`), accepted only if the new hash is an `manifest.accepted` variant |
    36	
    37	**The refusal rule.** A deployed file whose hash is neither the incoming one, nor the
    38	manifest row, nor an accepted variant, nor a hash in an attic manifest is a hand patch: the
    39	install stops with exit 4 and names the file. `--force` is the only way past and keeps the
    40	patch in the attic. This is what makes "never edited on the host" checkable rather than a
    41	convention.
    42	
    43	**Version stamping.** Every installed tool prints `tool=<name> version=<sha>` as its first
    44	log line, where `<sha>` is `short=` from `owner-bin/tools-version`. Lane markers
    45	(`.done` / `.needs-attention`) carry the same string, so a lane log names the code that
    46	produced it, and the daemon's marker-clearing rule can key on "the installed tools-version
    47	is newer than the marker". The PATH shim is the one exception: its stdout is the worker's
    48	stream, so it prints nothing.

    50	## What is installed, and where the truth lives
    51	
    52	| Installed as `owner-bin/…` | Source of truth | Why it is deployed rather than run from the checkout |
    53	|---|---|---|
    54	| `install.sh` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh` | so `--verify` / `--record` work on the host with no checkout |
    55	| `install-crons.sh` | idem | regenerates the crontab |
    56	| `owner-pause.sh` | idem | drives tmux, the crontab and the process table |
    57	| `owner-resume.sh` | idem | idem |
    58	| `owner-say.sh` | idem | drives tmux |
    59	| `goal-keeper.sh` | idem | long-running host loop |
    60	| `estimate.sh` | idem | cron job |
    61	| `status-snapshot.sh` | idem | host census |
    62	| `accounts.sh` | idem (work item W10) | the owner's command for the live accounts file; usable while the checkout is mid-merge, which is exactly when a key goes bad |
    63	| `stack-watch.sh` | idem | long-running host loop |
    64	| `capacityd.sh` | idem (work item W3) | 60 s controller loop; started by `install.sh --start-loops`, by `owner-resume.sh` and by a five-minute crontab row; single-instance under a lock |
    65	| `merge-daemon.sh`, `merge.sh`, `daemon-scan.py`, `daemon.conf` | idem (work item W5) | long-running host loop; must survive a mid-merge checkout. It is also the **runner of `local/bin/janitor.sh`** (every `janitor_interval_s`, detached and self-locking): the dead-session, parked-lane, stale-lane and spool passes have no other caller |
    66	| `codex` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex` **rendered** | a PATH shim by construction; the deployed copy is regenerated by `run_mode.py set speed` |
    67	
    68	Everything else stays in the checkout and is invoked by its **primary-checkout path**:
    69	`local/bin/{dispatch,lane,ci,review,autofix,checked-push}.sh`,
    70	`local/bin/{run_mode,capacity_controller,ready_report,estimate_post,pr_janitor,pr_merge}.py`.
    71	A worktree copy of a pipeline script can predate a protocol fix, so a worktree path is
    72	never used for them.
    73	
    74	### The owner's personal cron scripts
    75	
    76	These stay in `~/bin` on the host — they are the owner's, not the pipeline's — and
    77	`install-crons.sh` writes their crontab rows only when the run mode asks for them
    78	(`cron.watchdog`, `cron.heartbeat`, `cron.astra_poll`; all `off` since 2026-09-09).
    79	
    80	| Host path | Source of truth | Status |
    81	|---|---|---|
    82	| `~/bin/qpbt-watchdog.sh` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/qpbt-watchdog.sh` | cron row off since 2026-09-09 |
    83	| `~/bin/owner-heartbeat-check.sh` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-heartbeat-check.sh` | cron row off since 2026-09-09 |
    84	| `~/bin/astra-poll.sh` | `results/telemetry/owner-tools/astra-poll.sh` | cron row off since 2026-09-09 |
    85	| `~/bin/estimate.sh` | **retired** — superseded by `owner-bin/estimate.sh` | the crontab row now points at `owner-bin/` |
    86	
    87	## The owner's five commands
    88	
    89	```sh
    90	owner-bin/owner-pause.sh  [--deadline 15m] [--reason "..."] [--dry-run]
    91	owner-bin/owner-resume.sh [--dry-run] [--force-crontab]
    92	owner-bin/owner-say.sh --mode idle|interrupt|terminal [--timeout N] "TEXT"
    93	owner-bin/install-crons.sh [--paused] [--dry-run] [--restore FILE]
    94	owner-bin/accounts.sh     list | get | set | enable | disable | add | remove | probe | log
    95	```
    96	
    97	### `accounts.sh` — the keys, their ceilings and their health
    98	
    99	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is the **live** source of truth for
   100	admission: one entry per key, `{name, label, endpoint, codex_home, ceiling,
   101	external_reserved, enabled, note}`, any number of endpoints and keys. The capacity
   102	controller and `account_router.py` re-read it every tick and every reservation, so an edit
   103	reaches admission within 60 seconds with **no session prompted, no brief re-applied and
   104	nothing restarted**. `run_mode.py apply` seeds the file from the brief when it is absent and
   105	never overwrites an existing one.
   106	
   107	```sh
   108	accounts.sh list                                  # every key, its ceiling and its state
   109	accounts.sh set second ceiling 20                 # the admin took slots back
   110	accounts.sh set second reserved 4                 # a forked session shares this key
   111	accounts.sh disable second --note "quota gone"    # cap 0 immediately, no probes
   112	accounts.sh enable second
   113	accounts.sh add third --endpoint api.third.example \
   114	    --codex-home ~/.codex-third --ceiling 8       # routable at the next reservation
   115	accounts.sh remove third
   116	accounts.sh probe second                          # one read-only health probe, now
   117	accounts.sh log -n 20                             # who changed what, and when
   118	```
   119	
   120	* **`ceiling` is a ceiling, never a target.** The controller's AIMD discovery runs below it
   121	  and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`. Lowering it takes effect at the next
   122	  tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue — the cap does not leap to the new
   123	  number. A run sitting at 60 % of the ceiling with no refusals is behaving correctly.
   124	* **`external_reserved == ceiling` is legal** and means the key has no slot for the pipeline
   125	  right now — an honest state during a run, and different from `enabled: false`, which is a
   126	  decision.
   127	* **No key value is ever stored.** An entry names the codex home the key lives in; the
   128	  secret stays in that directory, which only the owner touches.
   129	* Every write is atomic (temp file + rename) and appends one line to
   130	  `watchdog/capacity/accounts.log`. A bad field is refused with the field named and the file
   131	  is left byte-identical, so the controller reading it a millisecond later never sees a
   132	  half-file.
   133	
   134	**From GitHub, when there is no shell.** A comment on the owner inbox issue in the fixed
   135	form `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]` (one or more lines
   136	per comment) is applied by `local/bin/janitor.sh` at its next sweep and answered with one
   137	reply saying exactly what took effect (`applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20`, or `rejected: …`
   138	with the reason). Only comments written by the repository owner login recorded in
   139	`local/README.md` are applied; anyone else's are answered with a `rejected:` line naming
   140	them. The channel carries `ceiling`, `reserved`, `enabled` and `note` only — an endpoint or
   141	a codex home is a path on the host and is set here, where a typo cannot travel through a
   142	public comment.
   143	
   144	**Measured health.** A key that answers `401`/`403`/invalid-key or `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`
   145	disables itself at the first occurrence, and an endpoint answering 5xx three times in two
   146	minutes does the same; both record the REASON in `watchdog/capacity/health.json` and cap the
   147	key at 0. A disabled key probes its own way back (read-only, bounded, single-flight) and
   148	returns at cap 1, never at its pre-outage cap. The hourly readiness report on the progress
   149	issue carries one line per key — ceiling, effective cap, live, refusals in the last ten
   150	minutes, health with its reason, and the owner's own note — so none of this needs a question
   151	to a session.
   152	
   153	### `owner-pause.sh` — pause within the deadline
   154	
   155	The deadline comes from `run.pause_deadline_min` in the run brief; no timestamp is written
   156	into the script. `--dry-run` prints the phase plan and the computed deadline and touches
   157	nothing.
   158	
   159	| T | Phase |
   160	|---|---|
   161	| +0:00 | `run_mode.py pause` — caps to 0, pre-pause caps saved **inside** `capacity/state.json`; `touch watchdog/drain` |
   162	| +0:30 | queued dispatches release themselves at the drain (none is killed); keeper, merge daemon, stack-watch and **capacityd** stopped by stop file (**kept**) and by a pid the script verifies against `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` first — a paused pipeline has no daemons running, and on a 128-core host shared with other users a recycled pid is real |
   163	| +1:00 | exactly one `owner-say.sh --mode terminal`: closing progress comment and handoff, no prose on the estimate issue, **no auto-resume** |
   164	| +2:00 | `crontab -l` backed up verbatim to `$W/crontab.<ts>.bak` (the phase fails if it returns nothing), then the paused crontab installed from a file under `$W` |
   165	| D−2:00 | leftovers killed with anchored patterns only, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 20 s; partial work stays in the worker's worktree, never `git clean` |
   166	| D−0:01 | "Goal paused" confirmed in the pane, `watchdog/pause-state.json` written, `stages.jsonl` and an `events.d/` entry appended, telemetry committed and published through `checked-push.sh`. One minute **before** the deadline, so a publish that takes a few seconds still finishes inside "within 15 minutes" |
   167	
   168	`watchdog/pause-state.json` is the single record: caps (**from run-mode, not from the
   169	already-zeroed live files**), speed, estimate cadence, crontab backup path and both
   170	sha256s, daemon PAR, the whole run mode, the measured limits, the main goal state and
   171	`paused_at`. It is written twice — a provisional copy (`status: pausing`) as soon as the
   172	caps are known, so a pause that dies mid-way still leaves the one number the resume cannot
   173	reconstruct, and the complete one (`status: paused`) after the telemetry is published, so
   174	it also lists the phases that failed at the very end. A deadline shorter than the nominal
   175	plan clamps the later phases onto it instead of running past it; the printed plan says so.
   176	
   177	### `owner-resume.sh` — restore from that record only
   178	
   179	`run_mode.py resume` for caps and speed; the crontab restored **verbatim** from the
   180	recorded backup with no `sed` un-commenting (the 2026-09-12 script's
   181	`sed -E 's#^\#PAUSED-2026[0-9]{4} ##'` would have resurrected the watchdog, astra-poll and
   182	heartbeat rows that have been deliberately off since 2026-09-09); a refusal with a printed
   183	diff when the live crontab is not the one the pause installed; **capacityd**, daemon,
   184	stack-watch and keeper restarted and every stop file removed; one resume message rendered
   185	from `run_mode.py show`. Then a post-condition check that fails loudly: every cap file
   186	exists, is numeric and nonzero for an account the brief enables (queried as
   187	`run_mode.py get enabled.<account>`, whose answer is `yes`/`no` — a briefed
   188	`enabled: false` account is skipped, not reported as a failure), no account is `down`, a
   189	capacity controller and a merge daemon are actually running, and `watchdog/drain` is gone.
   190	A resume that leaves no controller running exits 5: its caps could never move again.
   191	
   192	### `owner-say.sh` — one message, three modes
   193	
   194	* `idle` — wait for idle, never interrupt a turn.
   195	* `interrupt` — Escape after the grace, send, then `/goal resume`.
   196	* `terminal` — write `watchdog/goal-hold` **first**, Escape, send, and do **not** resume.
   197	  On 2026-09-12 the terminal stop order at 08:19Z was followed by an automatic goal resume
   198	  at 08:24Z; `goal-hold` is what stops `goal-keeper.sh` from doing that.
   199	
   200	Idleness is judged on the **last four non-empty lines** of the pane only. A stale
   201	"esc to interrupt" line in the scrollback made the previous version wait 20 minutes
   202	(2026-09-12 04:01Z–04:21Z).
   203	
   204	### `goal-keeper.sh`
   205	
   206	Two-minute tick: resume a stalled or paused goal, set the goal on a goal-less idle session,
   207	Escape a turn longer than `turn_max_min` (8 minutes in fast mode), and **drain
   208	`watchdog/main-inbox/`** so a dispatch nudge never waits for a long turn to end. The goal
   209	text is rendered from `run_mode.py show --oneline`; no cap, issue number or turn limit is
   210	written into the script. It does nothing at all while `watchdog/goal-hold` exists.
   211	
   212	Inbox file format: one message per file, one line; an optional first line
   213	`#mode: idle|interrupt|terminal` picks the delivery mode (default `interrupt`). Delivered
   214	files move to `main-inbox/sent/`.
   215	
   216	### `install-crons.sh`
   217	
   218	Regenerates the managed block of the crontab from the run mode — the estimate row at
   219	`estimate_cadence_min` (30 minutes in fast mode, 6 hours otherwise), the readiness report
   220	hourly and a five-minute row that restarts `capacityd.sh` if it is not running (the loop
   221	takes a lock, so the row can never create a second controller). The readiness and capacityd
   222	schedules are fixed policy, not brief fields — there is no `cron.<name>` knob, and nothing
   223	here reads one. The watchdog, heartbeat and astra-poll rows have been deliberately off since
   224	2026-09-09 and are written as comments saying so. Every other line of the live crontab is
   225	carried through verbatim, **including commented-out lines**: a `#PAUSED-…` row carries a
   226	schedule someone will want back, and dropping it would leave that schedule only in a backup
   227	file. It always backs up first (to
   228	`$W/crontab.<ts>.install.bak`, a name distinct from the pause's own
   229	`$W/crontab.<ts>.bak`, so an install a second later cannot overwrite the file
   230	`pause-state.json` points at), always installs from a file under `$W`, never `sed`s the
   231	live crontab, and **fails if `crontab -l` returns nothing** — which is what a wipe looks
   232	like, and one happened on 2026-09-12 through a `#` delimiter inside an `s#…#…#` expression.
   233	`--restore FILE` installs a file verbatim through the same guarded path; that is how
   234	`owner-resume.sh` puts the pre-pause crontab back.
   235	
   236	### `estimate.sh`
   237	
   238	Cheap enough for a 30-minute cadence: open PRs come from the committed read-only
   239	`results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-pulls.json` instead of up to 100 `gh pr view` calls
   240	(the in-PR count is labelled as snapshot-derived, with the snapshot's age), the branch diffs
   241	run in a throwaway worktree under the cache root instead of dirtying the primary checkout's
   242	`FETCH_HEAD` under `checked-push.sh`, the 24-hour-ago site count is cached for the clock
   243	hour, the whole run is wrapped in `timeout`, and the body is rendered by
   244	`local/bin/estimate_post.py`, the single writer of the estimate issue. The denominator
   245	stays 197 and the `<sub>` provenance line stays, so `estimates.jsonl` remains comparable
   246	across the whole series.
   247	
   248	### `owner-bin-codex` — the PATH shim template
   249	
   250	The deployed `owner-bin/codex` is **generated** from this template. `run_mode.py set speed
   251	fast|default` rewrites the single `@speed-args@` line to add or drop
   252	`-c 'service_tier="priority"'` and then calls `install.sh --record codex`; both renderings
   253	are recorded in `manifest.accepted`, which is why the regenerated file is not mistaken for a
   254	hand patch. This replaces the 2026-09-12 `speed-fast.sh` / `speed-default.sh` string
   255	surgery, which asserted an exact 90-character substring of a generated file.
   256	
   257	The shim does **not** rewrite the model. The `gpt-5.6-sol → gpt-6-astra` rewrite it used to
   258	carry made `sessions.jsonl` record a model that never ran; a run-wide override belongs in
   259	`models.override` in the run brief, where telemetry can see it.
   260	
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# install.sh — the ONE deployment path for the operator tools (design full-speed-v2 §7).
     3	#
     4	# Operator scripts drive tmux, the crontab and the host process table, so they cannot be
     5	# run from the checkout (which is mid-merge for minutes at a time).  They are therefore
     6	# COPIED to ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/ by this installer and never edited on the
     7	# host: on 2026-09-12 three versions of the lane runner ran at once, `merge-daemon-v9h.sh`
     8	# called a `/tmp/merge-v2.sh` that does not exist, and the shim was patched by an
     9	# `assert old in s` here-doc against a 90-character substring.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--start-loops] [--dry-run]
    13	#   install.sh --verify                 # dependency/hash check (the merge daemon's gate)
    14	#   install.sh --record <name>          # re-record a regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed)
    15	#
    16	# Options:
    17	#   --force        overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version.
    18	#                  The previous copy is MOVED to owner-bin/attic/<ts>/, never deleted.
    19	#   --start-loops  start capacityd.sh (the 60 s capacity controller loop) if it is not
    20	#                  already running and no stop file holds it.  Without a running
    21	#                  controller nothing writes watchdog/max-codex-*, the caps stay frozen
    22	#                  at whatever seeded them, there is no AIMD, no 5xx trip and no
    23	#                  half-open probe — the 2026-09-12 situation, recovered by hand — and on
    24	#                  a fresh host lane.sh:wait_for_slot fails closed with
    25	#                  `no-capacity-record`.  The merge daemon and the goal keeper are NOT
    26	#                  started here: owner-resume.sh owns those (design §5).
    27	#   --compat-tmp   create /tmp/<name> SYMLINKS into owner-bin/ so anything still invoking
    28	#                  a historical /tmp path runs versioned code.  Nothing is ever written or
    29	#                  edited in /tmp; an existing regular file there is refused, not clobbered.
    30	#   --crons        run install-crons.sh afterwards (crontab regenerated from run-mode).
    31	#   --dry-run      print the plan and touch nothing (implies --dry-run for --crons too).
    32	#   --dest DIR     install into DIR instead of $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin (tests).
    33	#   --compat-dir D create the compat symlinks in D instead of /tmp (tests).
    34	#   --speed S      render the PATH shim for speed S instead of asking run_mode.py (tests).
    35	#
    36	# What is written under owner-bin/:
    37	#   <tool>              the deployed copy, mode from the table below
    38	#   tools-version       describe= sha= short= installed_at= source= installer=  (one release)
    39	#   manifest.sha256     "<sha256>  <name>" for every file deployed now (sha256sum format)
    40	#   manifest.accepted   every hash this release accepts for a name; the PATH shim has two
    41	#                       (the fast and the default rendering), because run_mode.py set speed
    42	#                       regenerates it in place
    43	#   repo-root           the checkout this release was installed from
    44	#   attic/<ts>/         the previous copy of every file this run replaced, plus its manifest
    45	#
    46	# Refusal rule (the point of the installer): a deployed file whose hash is neither the
    47	# incoming one, nor the manifest row, nor an accepted variant, nor a hash recorded in an
    48	# attic manifest, is a HAND PATCH.  It is reported and the install stops with exit 4.
    49	# --force is the only way past, and it keeps the patch in the attic.
    50	#
    51	# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 --verify found a missing file or a hash mismatch ·
    52	#             4 a hand patch was refused · 5 a required source file is missing
    53	set -euo pipefail
    54	
    55	PROG="install.sh"
    56	
    57	usage() { sed -n '2,52p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    58	
    59	FORCE=0; COMPAT=0; CRONS=0; DRY=0; VERIFY=0; RECORD=""; START_LOOPS=0
    60	DEST=""; SPEED=""; COMPAT_DIR="${MIPSTARRE_COMPAT_DIR:-/tmp}"
    61	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    62	  case "$1" in
    63	    --force) FORCE=1 ;;
    64	    --compat-tmp) COMPAT=1 ;;
    65	    --crons) CRONS=1 ;;
    66	    --start-loops) START_LOOPS=1 ;;
    67	    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
    68	    --verify) VERIFY=1 ;;
    69	    --record) RECORD="${2:-}"; [ -n "$RECORD" ] || { echo "$PROG: --record needs a tool name" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
    70	    --dest) DEST="${2:-}"; [ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "$PROG: --dest needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
    71	    --compat-dir) COMPAT_DIR="${2:-}"; [ -n "$COMPAT_DIR" ] || { echo "$PROG: --compat-dir needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
    72	    --speed) SPEED="${2:-}"; [ -n "$SPEED" ] || { echo "$PROG: --speed needs fast or default" >&2; exit 2; }; shift ;;
    73	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    74	    *) echo "$PROG: unknown argument '$1'" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    75	  esac
    76	  shift
    77	done
    78	
    79	CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
    80	DEST="${DEST:-$CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin}"
    81	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
    82	
    83	# --- the checkout this installer belongs to --------------------------------------------
    84	# When install.sh is run from owner-bin (--verify / --record on the host) it cannot derive
    85	# the checkout from its own path, so fall back to the recorded repo-root.
    86	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    87	ROOT=""
    88	if [ -f "$SELF_DIR/../../../AGENTS.md" ]; then
    89	  ROOT="$(cd "$SELF_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    90	elif [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    91	  ROOT="$MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT"
    92	elif [ -r "$DEST/repo-root" ]; then
    93	  ROOT="$(cat "$DEST/repo-root")"
    94	else
    95	  ROOT="$HOME/MIPStarRE-qpbt"
    96	fi
    97	SRC="$ROOT/results/telemetry/owner-tools"
    98	
    99	sha256_of() {
   100	  local f="$1"
   101	  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$f" | awk '{print $1}'
   102	  elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 "$f" | awk '{print $1}'
   103	  elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then openssl dgst -sha256 "$f" | awk '{print $NF}'
   104	  else python3 -c 'import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$f"
   105	  fi
   106	}
   107	
   108	# name|source|mode|required — the inventory of §7.  "optional" entries belong to work items
   109	# that may not have landed yet (W3 capacityd, W5 merge daemon); a missing optional source is
   110	# a warning, a missing required source is a hard failure.
   111	tool_table() {
   112	  cat <<'TBL'
   113	install.sh|install.sh|755|required
   114	install-crons.sh|install-crons.sh|755|required
   115	owner-pause.sh|owner-pause.sh|755|required
   116	owner-resume.sh|owner-resume.sh|755|required
   117	owner-say.sh|owner-say.sh|755|required
   118	goal-keeper.sh|goal-keeper.sh|755|required
   119	estimate.sh|estimate.sh|755|required
   120	status-snapshot.sh|status-snapshot.sh|755|required
   121	accounts.sh|accounts.sh|755|required
   122	codex|owner-bin-codex|755|required
   123	stack-watch.sh|stack-watch.sh|755|optional
   124	capacityd.sh|capacityd.sh|755|optional
   125	merge-daemon.sh|merge-daemon.sh|755|optional
   126	merge.sh|merge.sh|755|optional
   127	daemon-scan.py|daemon-scan.py|755|optional
   128	daemon.conf|daemon.conf|644|optional
   129	TBL
   130	}
   131	
   132	# historical /tmp name|installed tool — --compat-tmp points every name the 2026-09-12 run
   133	# used at the one versioned copy.
   134	compat_table() {
   135	  cat <<'TBL'
   136	owner-say.sh|owner-say.sh
   137	owner-say-v3.sh|owner-say.sh
   138	owner-say-v4.sh|owner-say.sh
   139	owner-pause.sh|owner-pause.sh
   140	owner-pause-v2.sh|owner-pause.sh
   141	owner-pause-fast.sh|owner-pause.sh
   142	final-pause.sh|owner-pause.sh
   143	owner-resume.sh|owner-resume.sh
   144	goal-keeper.sh|goal-keeper.sh
   145	goal-keeper-v2.sh|goal-keeper.sh
   146	stack-watch.sh|stack-watch.sh
   147	stack-watch-v3.sh|stack-watch.sh
   148	merge-daemon.sh|merge-daemon.sh
   149	merge-daemon-v9h.sh|merge-daemon.sh
   150	merge.sh|merge.sh
   151	daemon-scan.py|daemon-scan.py
   152	estimate.sh|estimate.sh
   153	status-snapshot.sh|status-snapshot.sh
   154	TBL
   155	}
   156	
   157	# --- the PATH shim is GENERATED, not copied ---------------------------------------------
   158	# run_mode.py set speed regenerates the deployed shim from the same template by rewriting
   159	# its one SPEED_ARGS= line, so both renderings are released versions of `codex`.  The
   160	# rewrite is ANCHORED at the start of the line: the template documents both renderings in
   161	# its header, and a comment that merely shows the line must never be rewritten with it.
   162	SPEED_MARK='# @speed-args@ regenerated by run_mode.py set speed; do not edit by hand'
   163	render_shim() { # render_shim <fast|default> <src> <out>
   164	  local speed="$1" src="$2" out="$3" line n
   165	  case "$speed" in
   166	    fast) line="SPEED_ARGS=(-c 'service_tier=\"priority\"')   $SPEED_MARK" ;;
   167	    *)    line="SPEED_ARGS=()   $SPEED_MARK" ;;
   168	  esac
   169	  n="$(grep -c '^SPEED_ARGS=' "$src" || true)"
   170	  if [ "$n" != 1 ]; then
   171	    echo "$PROG: $src has $n lines starting with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required" >&2
   172	    exit 5
   173	  fi
   174	  awk -v repl="$line" '
   175	    /^SPEED_ARGS=/ { print repl; next } { print }' "$src" > "$out"
   176	}
   177	
   178	current_speed() {
   179	  local s=""
   180	  if [ -n "$SPEED" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$SPEED"; return 0; fi
   181	  s="$(python3 "${MIPSTARRE_RUN_MODE:-$ROOT/local/bin/run_mode.py}" get speed 2>/dev/null || true)"
   182	  s="$(printf '%s' "$s" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')"
   183	  case "$s" in
   184	    fast|default) printf '%s\n' "$s" ;;
   185	    *) if [ -r "$DEST/codex" ] && grep -q 'service_tier' "$DEST/codex" 2>/dev/null
   186	       then printf 'fast\n'; else printf 'default\n'; fi ;;
   187	  esac
   188	}
   189	
   190	manifest_hash() { # manifest_hash <name> [manifest]
   191	  { awk -v n="$1" '$2 == n { print $1 }' "${2:-$DEST/manifest.sha256}" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -n 1
   192	}
   193	
   194	known_hashes() { # every hash this installation accepts for <name>
   195	  local name="$1"
   196	  awk -v n="$name" '$2 == n { print $1 }' "$DEST/manifest.sha256" 2>/dev/null || true
   197	  awk -v n="$name" '$2 == n { print $1 }' "$DEST/manifest.accepted" 2>/dev/null || true
   198	  if [ -d "$DEST/attic" ]; then
   199	    find "$DEST/attic" -name manifest.sha256 -type f -print 2>/dev/null | while read -r m; do
   200	      awk -v n="$name" '$2 == n { print $1 }' "$m" 2>/dev/null || true
   201	    done
   202	  fi
   203	}
   204	
   205	VERSION="$( { sed -n 's/^short=//p' "$DEST/tools-version" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -n 1 )"
   206	echo "tool=$PROG version=${VERSION:-unreleased}"
   207	
   208	# --- --verify: the merge daemon's dependency gate ---------------------------------------
   209	if [ "$VERIFY" -eq 1 ]; then
   210	  rc=0
   211	  [ -r "$DEST/manifest.sha256" ] || { echo "$PROG: no manifest at $DEST/manifest.sha256; run install.sh" >&2; exit 3; }
   212	  while IFS='|' read -r name src mode req; do
   213	    [ -n "$name" ] || continue
   214	    want="$(manifest_hash "$name")"
   215	    if [ -z "$want" ]; then
   216	      if [ "$req" = required ]; then echo "$PROG: $name is not in the manifest" >&2; rc=3; fi
   217	      continue
   218	    fi
   219	    if [ ! -e "$DEST/$name" ]; then echo "$PROG: $name is missing from $DEST" >&2; rc=3; continue; fi
   220	    have="$(sha256_of "$DEST/$name")"
   221	    [ "$have" = "$want" ] || { echo "$PROG: $name hash $have does not match the manifest ($want)" >&2; rc=3; }
   222	  done <<EOF
   223	$(tool_table)
   224	EOF
   225	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then echo "$PROG: $DEST verified against the manifest"; fi
   226	  exit "$rc"
   227	fi
   228	
   229	# --- --record: re-record one regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed) -------------------
   230	if [ -n "$RECORD" ]; then
   231	  [ -e "$DEST/$RECORD" ] || { echo "$PROG: $DEST/$RECORD does not exist" >&2; exit 3; }
   232	  have="$(sha256_of "$DEST/$RECORD")"
   233	  ok=0
   234	  while read -r h; do [ "$h" = "$have" ] && ok=1; done <<EOF
   235	$(known_hashes "$RECORD")
   236	EOF
   237	  [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] || {
   238	    echo "$PROG: refusing to record $RECORD: hash $have is not a released version" >&2
   239	    echo "$PROG: regenerate it from $SRC or re-run install.sh --force" >&2
   240	    exit 4
   241	  }
   242	  if [ "$DRY" -eq 1 ]; then echo "$PROG: [dry-run] would record $RECORD $have"; exit 0; fi
   243	  tmp="$DEST/.manifest.$$"
   244	  awk -v n="$RECORD" '$2 != n' "$DEST/manifest.sha256" > "$tmp"
   245	  printf '%s  %s\n' "$have" "$RECORD" >> "$tmp"
   246	  LC_ALL=C sort -k2,2 "$tmp" -o "$tmp"
   247	  mv "$tmp" "$DEST/manifest.sha256"
   248	  echo "$PROG: recorded $RECORD $have"
   249	  exit 0
   250	fi
   251	
   252	# --- plan --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   253	[ -d "$SRC" ] || { echo "$PROG: no source directory $SRC" >&2; exit 5; }
   254	SPEED_NOW="$(current_speed)"
   255	echo "$PROG: source $SRC"
   256	echo "$PROG: dest   $DEST (speed=$SPEED_NOW$([ "$DRY" -eq 1 ] && echo ', dry run'))"
   257	
   258	STAGE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mipstarre-install.$$"
   259	mkdir -p "$STAGE"
   260	cleanup() { rm -rf "$STAGE"; }

1	# Protocol: full speed mode — the briefing, the mode file, the standing reports
     2	
     3	Normative for a *run*: a bounded period in which the fleet works at the owner's
     4	stated capacity and speed. Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first, then this file
     5	before starting or pausing a run.
     6	
     7	The rule this protocol exists to enforce: **the owner gives one briefing and
     8	afterwards receives only the estimate one-liner and the progress log.** Every
     9	number the owner states lives in exactly one file, and every component reads it
    10	through one tool. Nothing is transcribed by hand into a second place — on
    11	2026-09-12 the caps were restated five times, edited by hand ten times, and a
    12	resume script still announced "primary 5 / second 39 / total 44" forty minutes
    13	after those numbers were wrong.
    14	
    15	## 1. The briefing
    16	
    17	The owner copies the committed template
    18	`results/telemetry/owner-tools/run-brief.template.json` to
    19	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/run-brief.json` and edits the values. That is
    20	the **only** artifact the owner authors for a run.
    21	
    22	| Field | Meaning |
    23	|---|---|
    24	| `run.label` | free text, used in reports and telemetry |
    25	| `run.start` | ISO-8601 instant the run begins |
    26	| `run.dispatch_cutoff` | ISO-8601 instant after which no new dispatch starts (running work finishes), or the literal `until my word` for an open-ended run |
    27	| `run.pause_deadline_min` | the deadline budget for the pause procedure (section 6) |
    28	| `run.speed` | `fast` or `default` (section 5) |
    29	| `run.occupancy_target` | a fraction in `(0, 1]` of the effective cap; the integer floor everything quotes is `run_mode.py get floor` |
    30	| `run.progress_issue` | prose progress and the hourly readiness report |
    31	| `run.estimate_issue` | the two-line estimate, and nothing else, ever |
    32	| `run.owner_inbox_issue` | permission, credential, access and scope grants only |
    33	| `accounts[].name` | any name matching `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`; `primary` and `second` are ordinary entries, not a closed set |
    34	| `accounts[].label` | the human name of the key ("space", "relay-us7") |
    35	| `accounts[].endpoint` | the label failures and health are attributed to, so a key moved between homes keeps its identity |
    36	| `accounts[].codex_home` | that account's `CODEX_HOME` |
    37	| `accounts[].nominal_limit` | **a ceiling, never a target** (see below) |
    38	| `accounts[].external_reserved` | slots on that key the pipeline must not use (a forked session sharing the key), subtracted from the ceiling |
    39	| `accounts[].enabled` | `false` means the pipeline never dispatches there at all |
    40	| `models.override` | `null` = **resolve from `run.speed`** (section 5): `fast` means `astra-all`, `default` means the published `local/model-policy.json`. `"astra-all"` forces the hard model at any speed; `"policy"` keeps the published policy at any speed. Whatever is in force is recorded in telemetry |
    41	
    42	**Nothing else holds a capacity decision.** `accounts[].enabled` is the only
    43	statement of which keys a run may use, and `run_mode.py apply`, `pause` and
    44	`resume` DERIVE `watchdog/account-mode` from it (`both` when more than one
    45	account is enabled, `primary` otherwise). That file is what the deployed PATH
    46	shim reads before it lets a dispatch use a `CODEX_HOME` other than `~/.codex`;
    47	while it says `primary` every such dispatch exits 4 with `primary-only policy`.
    48	It was previously written by hand and nothing in the brief path touched it, so a
    49	brief that enabled `second` with a `nominal_limit` of 30 could hold a cap of 28
    50	and dispatch nowhere on that key, with the AIMD seeing only deaths — the
    51	idle-slot failure of 2026-09-12 intervention 2. Read it with `run_mode.py get
    52	account_mode`; `owner-resume.sh` exits 5 when the file and the brief disagree.
    53	Never edit it.
    54	
    55	## 1.1 The live accounts file
    56	
    57	The brief is **one-shot**; the set of usable keys is **live**. The owner's real situation is
    58	one to three endpoints, each with one or two keys, and each key's concurrency limit moving
    59	during the run: the endpoint's admin reassigns slots, the owner wins them back, a key
    60	becomes invalid, a key runs out of quota. On 2026-09-12 every one of those events reached
    61	the pipeline as a message to a session that had to be idle to receive it.
    62	
    63	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is therefore the source of truth for
    64	admission. One entry per key:
    65	
    66	```json
    67	{"schema": "mipstarre-accounts/1",
    68	 "accounts": [
    69	   {"name": "second", "label": "space", "endpoint": "api.finite-dimensional.space",
    70	    "codex_home": "~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy",
    71	    "ceiling": 30, "external_reserved": 2, "enabled": true, "note": ""}]}
    72	```
    73	
    74	| Field | Meaning |
    75	|---|---|
    76	| `name` | `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`; any number of entries |
    77	| `label` / `endpoint` | the human name, and the label failures and health are attributed to |
    78	| `codex_home` | that key's `CODEX_HOME`. **The key value itself is never in this file** — it lives in that directory, which only the owner touches |
    79	| `ceiling` | **a ceiling, never a target** (below) |
    80	| `external_reserved` | slots on the key the pipeline must not use. `external_reserved == ceiling` is legal and means the key has no slot for the pipeline right now — different from `enabled: false`, which is a decision |
    81	| `enabled` | `false` is cap 0 immediately and no health probe; removing the entry is the same |
    82	| `note` | the owner's own free text, echoed in the hourly per-key line and changing nothing |
    83	
    84	**`run_mode.py apply` seeds this file from the brief when it is absent and NEVER overwrites
    85	an existing one**, and where the file exists it is what `apply` reads. So re-applying a
    86	brief to change the speed tier, the cutoff or an issue number cannot undo an hour of ceiling
    87	edits; `rm` the file and re-apply to go back to the brief.
    88	
    89	**The controller and the router re-read it on every tick and every reservation** (at most
    90	60 s stale). Lowering a ceiling takes effect at the next tick; raising it lets the AIMD
    91	creep continue rather than jumping the cap; `enabled: false` and a removed entry are cap 0
    92	at once. An entry the owner adds gets its own cap file, its own health, its own
    93	`cap.<name>` accessor and its own line in every report, with nothing restarted.
    94	
    95	An **invalid** accounts file is a hard, named failure of the controller and admission; cap
    96	files remain untouched, and neither path substitutes the brief or historical homes.
    97	Read-only reports use the last-good run-mode snapshot. Pause may use that snapshot only to
    98	zero known caps; resume remains transactional and restores saved caps or stays paused.
    99	`ACCOUNTS:` comments update fields of a valid entry. Repairing malformed JSON or account
   100	structure is an explicit shell operation.
   101	
   102	A directive comment the janitor does not sweep within `accounts_inbox.py`'s staleness
   103	window (default 120 minutes, several sweeps wide) is **not** applied and **not** answered.
   104	No reply within a sweep means it did not take effect — repeat it.

   123	### The GitHub channel
   124	
   125	When the owner is away from a shell, a comment on the owner inbox issue
   126	(`run.owner_inbox_issue`) in the fixed form
   127	
   128	```
   129	ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false] [note=<word>]
   130	```
   131	
   132	— one or more lines per comment — is applied by `local/bin/janitor.sh`'s `owner-accounts`
   133	pass at its next sweep and answered with one reply per comment saying exactly what took
   134	effect: `applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20`, or `rejected: … — <reason>`. Three rules make
   135	it a control channel rather than a conversation:
   136	
   137	* only comments written by the **repository owner login** recorded in `local/README.md` are
   138	  applied (overridable with `MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN`); anyone else's are answered with a
   139	  `rejected:` line naming them, so an attempt is visible rather than silent;
   140	* a comment is applied **exactly once** — the reply carries
   141	  `<!-- mipstarre-accounts comment=<id> -->` and an answered comment is skipped — so a sweep
   142	  every minute cannot re-apply a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell;
   143	* the channel carries `ceiling`, `reserved`, `enabled` and `note` **only**. An endpoint or a
   144	  codex home is a path on the owner's host and is set with `accounts.sh`, where a typo
   145	  cannot travel through a public comment.
   146	
   147	Comment bodies are untrusted text (`issues-prs.md` §4): only `ACCOUNTS:` lines are read at
   148	all, every value is validated before anything is written, and nothing is interpolated into a
   149	shell.
   150	
   151	### Measured health
   152	
   153	A key is disabled by measurement, not by opinion. `401`/`403`/invalid-key and
   154	`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` disable it at the **first** occurrence — a `401` is not a statistic,
   155	and retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead sessions — and
   156	`endpoint_5xx` disables it at three deaths inside two minutes, the 2026-09-12 outage. Both
   157	write the reason into `watchdog/capacity/health.json`, one document for every key, and cap
   158	it at 0. The way back is the same half-open, single-flight, read-only probe in both cases,
   159	restoring cap **1** and letting AIMD climb; the key-invalid backoff starts at five minutes
   160	rather than thirty seconds, because a key does not become valid again in thirty seconds.
   161	`accounts.sh probe [name]` runs that probe now instead of waiting for the backoff.
   162	
   163	**`nominal_limit` is a ceiling and never a target.** It is the highest
   164	concurrency the key may ever reach. The controller may sit below it for the
   165	whole run and must never go above it; a run that sits at 60 % of the ceiling
   166	with zero refusals is behaving correctly, and "we are below the limit" is not a
   167	defect to report. The number to compare live workers against is the occupancy
   168	floor `run_mode.py get floor`, not the ceiling.

   170	## 2. Applying it
   171	
   172	### The run-start sequence, in order
   173	
   174	Applying the brief configures a run; it does not start one. This is the whole
   175	list — nothing else has to be remembered, and nothing here is optional:
   176	
   177	```bash
   178	local/bin/run_mode.py apply                                   # 1. the brief
   179	results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh --crons --start-loops # 2. tools, crontab, capacityd
   180	setsid nohup ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/merge-daemon.sh \
   181	    >> ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/lanes/daemon.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &   # 3. the merge queue
   182	setsid nohup ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/goal-keeper.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   183	setsid nohup ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/stack-watch.sh \
   184	    >> ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/lanes/stack-watch.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   185	tmux new -s qpbt 'local/bin/main-session.sh'                  # 4. the main session
   186	```
   187	
   188	Step 2 is the one that is easy to skip and impossible to notice: without a
   189	running `capacityd.sh` nothing writes `watchdog/max-codex-*` again, so there is
   190	no AIMD, no 5xx trip and no half-open probe — the caps stay frozen at whatever
   191	seeded them, which is exactly the 2026-09-12 situation the controller exists to
   192	remove — and on a fresh host `lane.sh`'s `wait_for_slot` fails closed with
   193	`no-capacity-record`. The five-minute crontab row installed in the same step
   194	brings the loop back if it is killed; `capacityd.sh` takes a lock, so a start
   195	that is already running is a no-op.
   196	
   197	After a pause, `owner-resume.sh` performs steps 1-3 from the pause record and
   198	checks afterwards that the controller and the daemon are actually running
   199	(exit 5 if not); only the main session is started by hand.
   200	
   201	### `run_mode.py apply`
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	local/bin/run_mode.py apply            # reads watchdog/run-brief.json
   205	local/bin/run_mode.py apply --brief PATH --dry-run
   206	```
   207	
   208	`apply` validates strictly and **fails loudly at briefing time rather than at
   209	05:00Z**. Each of these exits 2 naming the offending key, the template path and
   210	the destination path: an unknown key anywhere in the document, a missing or
   211	malformed `endpoint`, a non-integer limit, `external_reserved >=
   212	nominal_limit`, `occupancy_target` outside `(0, 1]`, an unknown `speed` or
   213	`models.override`, an issue number that is not a positive integer, the three
   214	issue numbers not being distinct, and an account named outside
   215	`{primary, second}`. A **missing brief is a hard error** naming the template and
   216	the exact destination — never "zero capacity" and never "unlimited".
   217	
   218	On success `apply`
   219	
   220	1. writes `watchdog/run-mode.json` atomically (temp file + `os.replace`);
   221	2. derives `watchdog/max-codex-primary`, `max-codex-second` and `max-codex`;
   222	3. regenerates the deployed PATH shim for the briefed speed (section 5);
   223	4. writes or removes `watchdog/model-override` from the **resolved**
   224	   `models.override` (section 5), which is what makes that field *do*
   225	   something: an override in force writes the runtime knob `model_policy.py`
   226	   reads, no override removes it. Validating the field is not applying it, and
   227	   until this step existed "every worker on the hard model" still needed a
   228	   hand-edited knob file or a reviewed PR mid-run;
   229	5. appends a `stages.jsonl` row carrying the brief's `sha256`;
   230	6. appends one row to `results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`.

   232	`run.main` (optional) carries the MAIN session's own launch values —
   233	`model`, `effort`, `codex_home` — read back by `local/bin/main-session.sh`
   234	through `run_mode.py get main.model|main.effort|main.codex_home`. Omitted, it
   235	defaults to `gpt-6-astra` / `xhigh` / the ambient `CODEX_HOME`; briefed, the
   236	brief wins, and the launcher prints which of the two it used.

   238	**The starting cap per account** is
   239	
   240	```
     1	# Protocol — admission capacity
     2	
     3	Normative for `local/bin/capacity_controller.py`, `local/capacity-policy.json` and the two
     4	admission inputs of `local/bin/account_router.py`.  Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first and

     8	The trigger is the full speed run of 2026-09-12.  The owner stated the concurrency limits
     9	four times, a person edited the cap files ten times (39 → 29 → 20 → 18 → 14 → 12 → 6 → 14 →

    13	
    14	## 1. What owns which number
    15	
    16	| Number | Owner | Where it lives |
    17	|---|---|---|
    18	| **Ceiling** — the most the pipeline may ever run on a key | the owner, live | `watchdog/accounts.json`, as `ceiling - external_reserved`; the run brief seeds that file once (`full-speed-mode.md` §1.1) |
    19	| **Cap** — how many it runs right now | the controller | `watchdog/capacity/state.json`, mirrored to the derived cap files |
    20	| **Floor**, AIMD constants, health thresholds | the reviewed policy | `local/capacity-policy.json` |
    21	| **Freeze** | the operator | `watchdog/capacity/hold` (touch file) |
    22	| **Zero** | the pause path | `capacity_controller.py pause` (never `echo 0 >`) |
    23	
    24	`ceiling_source` is validated to be `"accounts"` (or the historical `"brief"`), so a knob
    25	file can never raise the owner's limit.  The cap may sit below the ceiling forever and must
    26	never go above it.  **The accounts file is re-read on every tick and every reservation**, so
    27	a ceiling the owner lowers at 05:12Z is in force by 05:13Z with nothing restarted, and an
    28	entry they disable or remove is cap 0 with no probe.  An invalid accounts file is a hard,
    29	named failure with the cap files untouched — never a silent fall back to the brief, which
    30	would restore the ceiling the owner has just lowered.  Any number of named accounts:
    31	`primary` and `second` are ordinary entries, and nothing in the layer enumerates them.
    32	`external_reserved` is the owner's statement that something outside the pipeline shares the
    33	key (on 2026-09-12 a forked session, limited to two slots).  An **undeclared** sharer needs
    34	no identification: it appears as refusals, AIMD walks the cap down, and the gap is recorded
    35	as `external_inferred = nominal - external_reserved - measured_limit`.
    36	
    37	## 2. The control loop
    38	
    39	`results/telemetry/owner-tools/capacityd.sh` runs `capacity_controller.py tick` every 60 s —
    40	a `while`/`sleep` loop with a stop file and a single-instance lock, and nothing more.  It is
    41	**started** by `install.sh --start-loops`, restarted by `owner-resume.sh` phase 3 and brought
    42	back by the five-minute row `install-crons.sh` writes; copying the script is not running it,
    43	and with no controller the caps never move again.  Each tick, per account:
    44	
    45	1. **Counters** over the last `counter_window_s` (300 s), derived from the `failure_class`
    46	   and `endpoint` fields of `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`.  Never a grep of a capture:
    47	   the classification happens once, in `telemetry.py` (`classify_failure`, exposed to the
    48	   shell tools as `telemetry.py classify-failure`), and everything downstream reads it.
    49	2. **Additive increase.** `refusals_5m == 0` and `deaths_5m == 0` and `live >= cap - 1`,
    50	   held continuously for a full `quiet_window_s` → `cap += 1`.  One slot per window, never
    51	   more.  The `live >= cap - 1` term keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
    52	   of headroom.
    53	3. **Multiplicative decrease.** On the **first** refusal of a window,
    54	   `cap = max(floor, min(cap, live_at_first_refusal - 1))`; on any further refusal inside it,
    55	   `cap = max(floor, ceil(cap * decrease))`.  `live` is sampled at the tick that observes the
    56	   refusal, the closest the controller gets to the moment the provider said no.
    57	4. **Clamp** to `[floor, ceiling]`; when the two cross, the ceiling wins.
    58	5. **Neutral unknowns.** A `failure_class` the policy does not name, including the literal
    59	   `unknown`, is counted in neither direction.  It neither lowers the cap nor blocks the
    60	   climb, so a reworded provider message degrades to today's static behaviour — the cap
    61	   walks to the owner's ceiling and sits there, which is where a hand-set cap sat.  A
    62	   "treat unknown as a refusal" rule would instead collapse the cap the first time a
    63	   provider changed a string.
    64	
    65	Ordering inside a tick: health, then decrease, then increase, then the clamp, then the
    66	measurement.
    67	
    68	## 3. Endpoint health
    69	
    70	Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health, and a 5xx never runs
    71	the AIMD arithmetic.  `watchdog/capacity/health-<account>.json` holds
    72	`{state: up|degraded|down, since, consecutive_5xx, next_probe_at}` and the probe bookkeeping.
    73	
    74	- `fivexx_threshold` (3) `endpoint_5xx` deaths inside `fivexx_window_s` (120 s) → **down**,
    75	  and cap 0 at once.  This is the 05:30Z–05:58Z relay-us7 outage, answered on the day by a
    76	  human typing `echo 0`.
    77	- A **key-invalidating** class — any `failure_patterns` entry marked `"disables": true` other
    78	  than `endpoint_5xx`, today `auth` (401/403/invalid key) and `insufficient_balance`
    79	  (`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, quota) — → **down** at `disable_threshold` (1) occurrences.  One
    80	  `401` is the whole answer: no amount of AIMD makes an invalid key valid, and retrying it at
    81	  any concurrency produces nothing but dead sessions.  The backoff for this class starts at
    82	  `disable_backoff_s` (300 s) rather than 30 s, because a key does not become valid again in
    83	  thirty seconds.
    84	- Every trip records a **reason** (`reason`, `disabled_by`) in the health files.  "Cap 0"
    85	  with no reason is the state a person had to diagnose by reading captures on 2026-09-12;
    86	  the reason travels to `watchdog/capacity/health.json`, to `capacity_controller.py status`
    87	  and to the hourly per-key line on the progress issue.
    88	- Below the threshold but above zero → **degraded**: the cap is not cut, but the climb stops.
    89	- Recovery is half-open.  After `probe_backoff_s` (30 s, doubling to `probe_backoff_max_s`)
    90	  the controller runs **one** probe — `codex exec --sandbox read-only`, a trivial prompt,
    91	  that account's `CODEX_HOME`, bounded at `probe_timeout_s`, single-flight under
    92	  `watchdog/capacity/probe-<account>.lock`.  `probes_to_recover` (2) consecutive successes
    93	  leave `down` and restore cap **1**; one failure doubles the backoff.  **The cap never
    94	  jumps back to its pre-outage value** — an endpoint that just came back is the last thing
    95	  to hand twenty sessions.
    96	
    97	The health probe is a health check, not a work session: read-only, no persona, no task, no
    98	worktree write, nothing appended to `sessions.jsonl`; its record is the health file and the
    99	`capacity` / `endpoint-recovered` row in `stages.jsonl`.  It is the one `codex` invocation in
   100	the layer outside `dispatch.sh`, and it is confined to this paragraph.  That exception is
   101	also written into `local/protocols/meta.md` (Telemetry duties) and the AGENTS.md Sessions
   102	bullet, because a rule stated in one document and contradicted in another is not a rule;
   103	a second exception means amending all three in one commit.  The probe never fires while the
   104	run is paused, while `watchdog/capacity/hold` exists, or against a disabled account — a
   105	paused pipeline spends nothing on the owner's keys.
   106	
   107	`account_router.effective_caps` reads the health file and treats a `down` account as cap 0.
   108	Without that, `choose_account` *prefers* the dead account — it picks the lower live/cap
   109	ratio, and a dying endpoint keeps freeing slots — so an outage accelerates itself.  That is
   110	how one hour of 503s cost 69 sessions.
   111	
   112	**An invalid accounts file stops the controller and admission.** Both name the
   113	invalid file; neither substitutes historical homes or the brief. Cap files stay
   114	untouched. Read-only reports may use the last-good run-mode snapshot, and pause
   115	may use that snapshot only to zero known caps. Structural repair is an explicit
   116	shell operation, not an `ACCOUNTS:` field directive.
